516a4f414b98a975: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Malaysia’s manufacturing sector is expected to continue supporting industrial production and overall economic growth in the fourth quarter of 2026 (4Q 2026), according to MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB IB).

In a note today, MBSB said the positive outlook is supported by the strong new order growth, improving export demand and sustained hiring backed by Malaysia’s stronger-than-expected gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 5.3 per cent year-on-year in the third quarter of 2026 and a 53.7 per cent year-on-year expansion in trade in September.

It said Malaysia’s S&P Global Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 51.0 in October 2026 from 49.9 in September, returning to expansionary territory and marking the strongest improvement in manufacturing conditions since April 2026.
“The latest PMI reading signals continued growth in industrial production and overall economic activity in 4Q 2026,” it said.
The investment bank said stronger demand had encouraged firms to increase purchasing activity and sustain employment growth for a third consecutive month.
It said input cost inflation had accelerated due to higher transportation and raw material costs, partly linked to the West Asia conflict, prompting manufacturers to raise selling prices.
Nevertheless, MBSB IB said that rising input costs, persistent supply-chain disruptions and weaker business sentiment remain key downside risks.

“Ongoing geopolitical tensions in West Asia and elevated transportation costs could continue to exert pressure on manufacturers’ margins and contribute to higher producer price inflation moving forward,” it said. — Bernama

0e0ed93357257100: PUTRAJAYA: Parent-Teacher Associations (PTA) nationwide can submit applications directly to the Education Ministry (MOE) for maintenance and repairs to their respective schools' physical facilities for 2027.
The special application channel is open for a month, from Nov 1 to 30, allowing PTAs to list their schools' infrastructure repair needs for the ministry's consideration.

In a statement, MOE said the initiative followed the announcement of an increased allocation of RM2 billion for school maintenance under the 2027 Budget, an increase of RM1 billion from the previous allocation.
The ministry said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling the Budget on Oct 9, also announced the allocation to repair and maintain all types of schools nationwide.
"To this end, MOE has established a special channel for PTA to submit applications directly for their schools' maintenance and physical facility repair needs for 2027.
"Applications are open for a month, from Nov 1 to 30, through the link and QR code provided," the statement said.

Previously, on Aug 30, Anwar announced a 50 per cent increase in the school maintenance allocation, from RM1 billion to RM1.5 billion for 2027, during the 2026 National Day Prime Minister's Address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC).
He also directed MOE to conduct ground visits to every district to assess applications for school infrastructure repairs.
However, MOE stressed that the opening of the special application channel did not mean that all applications submitted would be automatically approved.
Instead, each proposal must be based on actual needs, with priority given to critical damage and issues involving the safety risks of pupils and school staff.
MOE hopes the facility will make it easier for PTAs to submit maintenance and repair applications for their respective schools directly to the ministry.
a047a3ec8c8cb419: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Planning to book dinner at Rembayung soon? With Grab Dine Out, you can now book a table at the highly popular restaurant.

Previously, Rembayung used Umai to manage its table reservations. However, securing a table was often a nightmare, as the booking system was frequently overwhelmed by heavy traffic, resulting in crashes and long delays in the virtual waiting room. Diners were also left waiting without real-time notifications when reservation slots were fully booked.
Khairul Aming teams up with Grab to counter scalpers

Previously, Khairul Aming says a lot of table or dining reservations were taken up by scalpers. The Kelantanese admitted this is a major issue because a lot of genuine customers missed out on their bookings.
Khairul Aming himself added that he was “stuck” when dealing with this issue, even declining the suggestion to include IC as a way to make bookings due to safety and privacy concerns.
Now, the local entrepreneur announced a partnership with Grab to address this issue. Khairul Aming said that booking a table Rembayung can now be done via Grab’s Dine Out feature.
What’s the difference between Umai and Grab?
For context, Umai is a cloud-based restaurant reservation and guest management (CRM) software that was used by Rembayung to handle bookings or reservations.

Through Umai’s system, bookings opened daily at 9pm (except Fridays) and it offered two-tiered windows for reservations. The first being short-term reservations (two days in advance) and longer-term bookings (up to two weeks in advance).

Additionally, the number of customers are limited to a minimum of two people per session or a maximum of eight people per session. Through Umai, your dining sessions are limited to around one hour 45 minutes to one hour 50 minutes.

Customers will also need to pay deposit of RM10 per person through the portal. The reservations are also limited to one booking per day, if the system found out a guest had double booked, the booking will be cancelled and the RM10 will not be refunded. This was done to ensure fairness for other customers.
Those who made a booking would also need to show their proof of purchase on email at the entrance.

On the other hand, Grab provides two options — Dine in and Take Away, depending on the guest’s preferences. If you want to dine in, you can make a booking via Grab Dine Out. Reservations open from 11am to 9pm. If customers want a take away meal, the booking options starts from 12:45pm to 6:45pm.

The number of diners per booking starts from a minimum of three people per session and caps at a maximum of eight people. Do keep in mind that children and babies are also considered as one person. For example, you can book a table for eight guests, that being four adults and four children.

Moreover, diners are only allowed one reservation within seven days before or after an active booking. Double booking would result in cancellation without refund. Like Umai, diners are also given one hour and 45 minutes for each dining session.

Besides that, diners can also make a special request such as strollers or wheelchairs, subject to availability and restaurant’s discretion. Should they be late to Rembayung, the restaurant will only hold the table for 15 minutes. Late comers would result in automatic cancellation with no refunds.

Rembayung also strictly forbid table swapping or transfer booking ownership to prevent scalpers from getting table reservations. Diners will need to present their proof of purchase directly to the PoC at the entrance. Remember, Rembayung does not accept screenshots as proof.
Currently, Rembayung only accepts cashless transactions like Debit, Credit card and QR only.
How you can use Grab Dine Out to book a table at Rembayung
Making dinner reservations at Rembayung through Grab Dine Out is quite straightforward. First, tap on the “Dine Out” feature, type “Rembayung” on the search bar, then tap “Book A Table”.
Customers can then choose their preferred number of pax, date and seating preference. After they are done, they will be led to the payment page and complete their payments there.
For diners based overseas such as Singapore, Indonesia and Brunei. They can still make a booking by switching their locations to Malaysia. — SoyaCincau
1b09ec73b621bf0c: LONDON, Nov 3 — A man who drugged and raped his wife over two decades and allegedly invited strangers to participate had “over a million photographs and videos” on his phone cataloguing the abuse, a UK court heard Monday.

The court in Manchester, northwest England, is hearing the trial of nine men accused of various sexual offences against a woman who was abused by her husband — a man in his 60s who cannot be named to protect the victim’s identity.
The husband filmed and shared images of the abuse on the “internet and social media applications” with “other like-minded men”, prosecutor Louise Oakley told the court.
Some of the defendants allegedly “hid behind a screen” and conspired with the husband over the years to administer substances to the woman so she could be “used and abused”.
And starting 2023, the prosecutor said, the husband began inviting men around to their home and filmed himself and others raping her while she was unconscious.

It is the second case involving a man accused of inviting strangers to take part in abusing his wife currently being heard in Britain. A trial in Winchester in the south involving four men opened last week.

Global awareness of the crime, known as organised drug-facilitated sexual assault (DFSA), has grown following the high-profile conviction in France of Dominique Pelicot, who drugged and raped his then-wife Gisele for nearly a decade alongside strangers.
Oakley told the jury in Manchester that the huband’s phone, which was seized when he was arrested, was like a “confession booth” including “barbaric sexual fantasies” going back to 2004.
“There were over a million photographs and videos cataloguing not only his abuse of his wife but abuse on her committed by others, including those in the dock today,” Oakley said.
“There is no doubt he lived a double life masked in respectability,” the prosecutor said.
The husband pleaded guilty in September to some 60 sexual offences against his wife including administering a substance with intent to stupefy or overpower her.
He and 13 other men are accused of conspiring to abuse the woman. Four of the men have since pleaded guilty to various offences.
The remaining nine men, aged between 28 and 70, deny various charges including rape, sexual assault and conspiracy to administer a statement substance with intent.
They include a taxi driver, a recruitment agency worker, a building supplies worker and a senior medic. — AFP
beac65a02670f313: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 3 — Johor’s rapid expansion of data centres has reportedly raised concerns among residents in Iskandar Puteri over noise, environmental conditions and the potential impact of nearby infrastructure on property values.

According to Singapore’s The Straits Times, some homeowners are considering selling their properties following the construction of data centres and high-voltage transmission towers near residential neighbourhoods.

Among them is finance manager Lee Shi Qing, 38, who reportedly put her RM1 million terraced house in Eco Botanic up for sale after construction began on a nearby 64-megawatt data centre by TM Nxera, a joint venture involving Telekom Malaysia and Singtel’s Nxera.
“I do have some concerns about living close to high-voltage lines, which is part of why I’m selling,” she told the Singapore newspaper.

Johor-based property consultant Samuel Tan reportedly warned that the presence of transmission towers could discourage potential buyers, even where scientific evidence does not establish a health risk.

The concerns come as Johor recorded 4,222 unsold completed homes and 9,946 unsold serviced apartments in the first half of 2026, the highest figures nationwide, according to the National Property Information Centre.

The state currently has 65 data centre projects at various stages of approval, while its operational IT capacity has reached 1,110MW, making it the Asia-Pacific region’s third-largest data centre market after Tokyo and Singapore, according to figures cited by The Straits Times.

Residents in Nusantara Prima and Nusa Bayu have also reportedly complained about construction dust, persistent humming noises and higher temperatures, which they believe are linked to nearby data centre developments.

Nusantara Prima kindergarten operator Mohanambal Rethinam told the newspaper that enrolment had fallen from 50 children in 2025 to 20 this year, with some parents expressing concerns about the surrounding environment.

Another resident, Nooraini Jaafar, 68, reportedly expressed concern that proximity to a data centre could make her terraced home harder to sell, despite its estimated value rising from RM400,000 in 2014 to RM600,000.
However, Universiti Teknologi Malaysia professor Mohd Fadhil Md Din cautioned against assuming that transmission lines posed a health risk to residents living hundreds of metres away.

“Where residences are genuinely 200m to 300m away, the scientific evidence would not support a blanket conclusion that residents are experiencing dangerous EMF exposure or that relocation is required on health grounds alone,” he told The Straits Times.
fb11c684f69b827d: WASHINGTON: The US Supreme Court on Monday rejected a Trump administration emergency bid to force California to set aside the mail-in ballots of more than 20,000 people on the grounds they may not be American citizens.

Acting a day before the US midterm elections, the top court denied the request in an unsigned, one-sentence ruling, as is common in urgent cases before the court. It gave no reasoning for the decision.

The federal government had accused California of having 190,000 illegal voters on its rolls. It recently revised the figure to 20,000 and filed an emergency lawsuit – after early voting had begun – to stop the state from sending ballots to them.
The Supreme Court action came after lower courts last week – and again on Monday – rejected the demand by the Department of Justice (DOJ), with one judge calling it brazen pre-election interference.

Solicitor General D. John Sauer, in an emergency filing with the Supreme Court, had said that "once California commingles the challenged ballots with lawful ones, there is no way to get the challenged ballots back."

The California ballot case appeared to be another attempt by the administration to cast doubt on the results of Tuesday's vote, in which President Donald Trump's Republican Party is at risk of losing control of Congress.
Trump – who has never acknowledged his own election defeat by Democrat Joe Biden in 2020 – has been claiming for months that there will be fraud in the midterms.
US District Judge David Carter last week refused to order the seizure of the ballots and sided with the government of Democratic-led California.
"The DOJ's actions are indicative of a broad, ongoing pattern of attempted election interference by federal officials," Carter said.
Another district judge, James Boasberg, also ruled against the Trump administration on Monday, saying the lists of alleged non-citizens were "flawed."

A controversy similar to California's arose in neighbouring Nevada. The administration said initially it had identified 16,000 non-citizen voters there, but after verification procedures that number dropped to 185 – and then to zero.
Studies repeatedly show that while cases of voter fraud exist, such incidents are extremely rare and do not influence election results.

In another closely-watched election case, a federal judge in Alaska over the weekend tossed out a bid by the Trump administration to hold up US Senate election results in the state should the Democratic candidate win.

The DOJ had asked the court to block certification of the results if Republican Dan Sullivan, the incumbent, loses on Tuesday because a second candidate also named Dan Sullivan would have siphoned off votes.

Mary Peltola, the Democratic candidate for Senate in Alaska, has denied recruiting the second Sullivan into the race, but The New York Times reported that members of her campaign staff had been involved.--AFP

fef0f760c5edae40: MASJID TANAH: Pakatan Harapan candidate for the Kuala Linggi seat, Mohammad Mukhlisul Mubin, wants to champion a performance- and service-based approach to politics rather than merely shaping public perception through campaigns.

The 25-year-old, better known as Muklis Mubin, said this approach must be reflected in efforts to address local issues, including fishermen's welfare, flooding, employment opportunities and internet connectivity, which still require attention.
He said these issues should not only be addressed by him but also collectively championed by all candidates contesting the election to ensure they receive attention at the appropriate level.
"We want to serve the people of Kuala Linggi wholeheartedly.

"To date, we have raised several local issues and are finalising them for inclusion in our manifesto," he told reporters after attending a programme with the fishing community in Kuala Linggi here last night.
He said the programme was aimed at bringing him closer to the community while gathering feedback on issues raised during previous engagements.
"The meeting with the fishing community provided a platform for us to update them on the progress of several matters raised previously.
"These include issues that have received positive feedback and approval, such as the reconstruction of the Telok Gong jetty, among others," he said.
On the challenges during the campaign period, Muklis acknowledged that he was still relatively new to politics and had many shortcomings to address.
However, he said all criticism, feedback and advice received, including through social media, would serve as guidance for him and his team to improve their approach.

"I admit that I still have many weaknesses and shortcomings because none of us is perfect. However, I am trying to introduce a new political approach in the country, namely performance-based politics rather than politics based solely on perception.
"We take criticism positively, while setting aside anything that is not constructive," he said.
Muklis said the response from Kuala Linggi constituents during his walkabouts had been very encouraging, with strong support for the voices of younger people.
He said the biggest challenge was meeting everyone's expectations, as every action taken would inevitably attract differing views and criticism.
"Nevertheless, I will take all feedback and criticism positively as an opportunity to improve myself and enhance the quality of service to the community," he said.
593a574c674dc71a: MANCHESTER, Nov 3 — Michael Carrick brushed off suggestions he has just two games left as Manchester United boss as he prepares his underperforming side for Tuesday’s Champions League clash against Roma.

Carrick’s position at Old Trafford is increasingly precarious following Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, which extended United’s winless run in all competitions to nine games — they last had a longer such sequence in 1984.
Former United and England midfielder Carrick was asked at his pre-match press conference on Monday whether he felt he had just two games remaining at the helm — against Roma and Aston Villa.
The Villa match on Sunday comes just before an international break, potentially giving the United hierarchy an opportunity to make a managerial change.
“No, not at all,” said the 45-year-old, in his first full season in charge. “If you look into the future, you never know what’s going to happen.
“I don’t know what’s going to happen. That doesn’t change the way I feel, how we’re preparing for the game tomorrow.
“I’m actually really looking forward to the game, can’t wait for the game tomorrow. You might think I’m crazy with the results we’ve had and what’s going on, but I genuinely can’t wait.”
Carrick also said he had “no concerns” over the commitment of out-of-form Argentine centre-back Lisandro Martinez, who was sent off in United’s defeat at Stamford Bridge.
The defender had previously criticised club chiefs over a lack of investment in the squad.

“Things happen in football, sometimes you do things, sometimes you make decisions, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you, but the commitment is not an issue for sure,” said Carrick.
Dressing room mood
The United head coach insisted the dressing room was in “a good place” despite the club’s terrible start to the season.
“Perception is a funny thing. You can make things look all sorts of different ways and think about all sorts of different things,” he said.

“I’ve said it before, the commitment of the players to the club, to me, to each other, I don’t question that at all. We need to play better, we can make better decisions, but commitment is not a thing at all.”
United are just one place above the Premier League relegation zone after taking a mere seven points from their nine matches so far this season.
And they are 20th in the Champions League table following a dismal 4-1 defeat away at Como last month. Only the top 24 teams will progress beyond the league phase.
But midfielder Kobbie Mainoo, sitting alongside Carrick at Monday’s press conference, said United could turn things around.
“We’ve not had the results we’ve wanted,” Mainoo said. “But we need to look forward now. There’s big, big games ahead and I feel like we’re one win away from changing that.”
Carrick has fond memories of facing Roma as a member of Alex Ferguson’s team, scoring twice in United’s 7-1 quarter-final second-leg triumph in the Champions League in 2007.
“It was a magical night, I have to say,” he recalled. “It was one of the best nights, one of the best games, one of the best atmospheres I’ve been fortunate enough to witness.”
Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini insisted Carrick’s men should not be underestimated despite their miserable form.
“Obviously Manchester United is struggling somewhat in terms of results in the Premier League at the moment,” he said.
“We can’t get distracted and too hung up on that situation because we know that United is a strong team. We know that they have top players in their squad.
“They make things very difficult for the opposition at Old Trafford, so we’ll be playing as if we’re against United at the top of its form.” — AFP
aac656d1759f46aa: LOS ANGELES: Two decades after releasing their landmark opus The Black Parade, American rock outfit My Chemical Romance have finally carried the record to the top of the Billboard 200.
The band's latest release, The Black Parade (20th Anniversary Deluxe Edition), hit the top spot, marking the group's first No.1 album in a nearly 25-year career.
According to Billboard, the lavish reissue moved 78,000 equivalent album units across more than 20 physical formats and variants to seal the victory.

Celebrating the milestone on social media, the group posted an Instagram story set to Miley Cyrus' hit track "Wrecking Ball"—a tongue-in-cheek nod to 2006, when Cyrus' Hannah Montana soundtrack narrowly denied The Black Parade the top spot during its original debut at No.2.

The original third studio album saw the New Jersey emo pioneers dramatically expand their sound, crafting an ambitious rock opera heavily influenced by Queen that spawned the iconic Top 10 single "Welcome to the Black Parade".
Over the past two decades, the record has cemented its status as one of the definitive 21st-century rock albums.
This latest chart success follows the expanded package's release on Oct 23, which also earned the group their inaugural No.1 on the UK's Official Albums Chart just days prior.
Notably, the 20-year-old masterpiece managed to edge out pop megastar Olivia Rodrigo's latest effort, You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love.
Rodrigo proved a gracious competitor, posting a clip on Instagram from a My Chemical Romance concert she attended at New York's Citi Field earlier this year alongside a celebratory tag for the band.
The chart triumph arrives midway through the group's extensive Long Live the Black Parade stadium tour, which commenced in 2025.
Fans in Malaysia will see the band perform live in Kuala Lumpur on Nov 19 and 20 at TM Stadium Nasional in Bukit Jalil.
bdaa67e05373bf29: MELAKA: Amanah is confident of winning all seven seats it is contesting in the state election, its president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said.
Its president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the confidence was in line with Pakatan Harapan's target of winning 18 of the 24 seats it is contesting.
"Amanah is contesting seven state seats and we are confident of winning all seven," he said.
He was speaking at a press conference after attending a PH campaign programme in Telok Gong here last night.
On PH's selection of young candidates, Mohamad said the coalition continued to enjoy support from the younger generation while also providing opportunities for candidates from different age groups.
He said young candidates deemed qualified and capable should be given the opportunity to serve and represent the public.
"PH has no shortage of support from young people. That is why we identify young people whom we consider qualified and capable and introduce them to the public.
"I was 27 when I first became a candidate," he said.
The agriculture and food security minister said the emphasis on young candidates did not mean veteran politicians were being sidelined, as PH represented people from all age groups.
On the turnout of supporters during nomination day, Mohamad said the number of people present did not necessarily reflect the actual level of voter support on polling day.
He said he had experienced a similar situation when he was with Pas, where a large turnout of supporters on nomination day did not necessarily guarantee victory.
He also expressed hope that the wave of support currently perceived to be favouring Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional would not influence voters' decisions on Nov 14.
"That is our hope. We are confident that the people of Melaka will make a different choice from what happened in the previous two states," he said.
PH is targeting 18 of the 24 seats it is contesting in the Melaka election, including retaining the five seats it won previously.
The coalition's candidates comprise 10 from PKR, while DAP and Amanah have seven candidates each.
885bdb34dc5f776f: SINGAPORE, Nov 3 — The government will face questions in Parliament today on its response to transboundary haze, plans to revamp the car ownership system and the resilience of public healthcare services following a major IT disruption.

The sitting will also cover child-protection measures following the death of an eight-month-old baby who was repeatedly abused by his parents, with MPs submitting questions across these issues, CNA reported.
Haze response under scrutiny

The haze, which has affected Singapore’s air quality since September, has prompted questions about whether existing legislation can effectively address pollution originating from forest fires in Indonesia and whether companies linked to the fires can be held responsible.

Authorities have since formed a joint task force with Indonesia to investigate companies suspected of involvement, issued notices to Singapore-based firms under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act (THPA) for the first time, and indicated that existing laws could be amended or new legislation introduced.

MP Tin Pei Ling (PAP-Marine Parade-Braddell Heights GRC) wants to know what action has been taken against companies with direct or indirect responsibility for the fires, while MP Sylvia Lim (WP-Aljunied GRC) is seeking an explanation for why investigations into four companies over possible THPA breaches, opened in 2015, have yet to be concluded.

MP Sharael Taha (PAP-Pasir Ris-Changi GRC) has proposed a coordinated approach involving relevant agencies to investigate companies, identify their ultimate owners and financial links, and establish accountability, while MP Jamus Lim (WP-Sengkang GRC) is asking how many licensed preschools lack air-conditioned indoor areas and how their preparedness for haze conditions is checked.
MP He Ting Ru (WP-Sengkang GRC) will also use an adjournment motion to discuss how Singapore can strengthen its part in addressing transboundary haze.
COE reform and car affordability

The Land Transport Authority’s proposal to combine car COE Categories A and B into a single category, with surcharges and rebates linked to a vehicle’s open market value, has prompted MPs to question how the changes would affect buyers.

MP Yip Hon Weng (PAP-Yio Chu Kang SMC) is seeking details on the market distortion the proposed arrangement is meant to address and how its effectiveness in distinguishing mass-market cars from higher-value models will be measured, while MP Jessica Tan (PAP-East Coast GRC) wants the review to account for the needs of families and small and medium-sized enterprises that depend on cars or commercial vehicles, including those unable to afford ownership under market-driven COE prices.

MP Edward Chia (PAP-Holland-Bukit Timah GRC) has also asked why the proposed fees and rebates are calculated as a proportion of the COE price rather than set at fixed amounts, and how buyers will be protected from dealers incorporating rebates into their selling prices.
Public healthcare system outage

The nine-hour interruption to services across Singapore’s three public healthcare clusters on October 13 has also drawn questions about the reliability of shared IT infrastructure and the arrangements for restoring services when systems fail.
The outage resulted from a technical problem affecting network connectivity, although national health technology agency Synapxe said there was no indication that it involved a cyber incident.

Nominated MP Haresh Singaraju is asking whether the system has an independent backup, how quickly it is supposed to be restored and whether that recovery target was achieved, while MP Joan Pereira (PAP-Tanjong Pagar GRC) wants figures on the number of patients affected and an explanation of why backup infrastructure did not prevent the disruption; MP Cassandra Lee (PAP-West Coast-Jurong West GRC) is seeking an update on the investigation and possible measures to reduce the risk of similar interruptions.
Child-protection safeguards

The case of an eight-month-old infant who died in September 2024 after repeated abuse by his parents, both jailed on October 21, has prompted three MPs to question how warning signs involving very young children are detected before cases escalate.

Nominated MP Kenneth Poon is asking how suspected abuse involving children aged three and below who are not already known to social services can be identified, and how the Ministry of Social and Family Development connects separate concerns raised by caregivers and professionals to ensure timely intervention.

Nominated MP Neo Kok Beng wants to know whether the Sensemaking Alerts for Frontline Engagement and Response (SAFER) system could have identified cases of this nature and what additional measures would be considered if it could not, while MP Choo Pei Ling (PAP-Chua Chu Kang GRC) is asking whether information from young children’s healthcare visits could be included in SAFER’s cross-agency risk assessments and how repeated medical visits or suspected non-accidental injuries are followed up.
b72f36025a2c8f09: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — When Tan Shing Win made coffee outdoors, he noticed something that kept bothering him: the same beans and brewing recipe could produce a different cup depending on the environment.

It was an everyday observation, but one that eventually helped shape his presentation at the 2026 World Barista Championship (WBC) in Panama, where he finished second — the best result ever achieved by a Malaysian competitor.
Moisture became the focus of his routine, reflecting a question that had followed him through years of making coffee in different settings.

“Sometimes, even when using the exact same brewing recipe, the results could be quite different depending on the environment,” Shing Win says. “This made me wonder how factors such as humidity might be influencing the way we brew coffee.”
Moisture, he explains, is not often a major topic of discussion in coffee brewing. Yet it was something his team paid attention to when adjusting coffee for different environments.

“Over time, I became more curious about how something we often overlook could influence the way we make coffee. That curiosity eventually led me to explore moisture more deeply and make it the central idea of my routine.”
The approach is characteristic of Shing Win: technical, observant and more interested in pursuing a question than presenting an elaborate story.
That quality is familiar to his coach, Keith Koay, who first met him in 2016, shortly after opening a coffee shop in Taman Paramount, PJ.

(That little coffee shop, of course, is none other than One Half Coffee; it would eventually pave the way for other now-veteran establishments in the local F&B scene, such as Dou Dou Bake and One Half Roastery.)
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Tan Shing Win’s WBC approach was technical, observant and more interested in pursuing a question than presenting an elaborate story. — Picture courtesy of Tan Shing Win
“He came in as a customer, curious about coffee and searching for answers about a career path that was still quite blurry to him,” Keith recalls.
He eventually hired Shing Win as a part-timer. What stood out was not necessarily his talent, but his attitude towards learning.
“He was never in a rush to prove himself. Instead, he was happy to observe, learn humbly behind the bar, and build his understanding of coffee from the ground up.”
Keith, himself a three-time Malaysian Barista Champion (winning the titles in 2016, 2018 and 2020), says Shing Win was willing to dedicate time to the craft without expecting immediate results.
Those early qualities, he believes, helped bring the barista to the world stage.

“One question we kept coming back to throughout our preparation was: ‘We want to see someone who can change or inspire the coffee industry. Do you think what you’re presenting in these 15 minutes truly represents that?’” Keith says.
Sometimes, Shing Win’s response was silence. Keith felt that, deep down, he knew when the answer was no.

“So we went back, questioned our ideas, and continued refining the routine. It wasn’t necessarily about finding something more impressive to present, but making sure that everything we put on stage had a purpose and something meaningful to contribute.”

The moisture concept emerged from an ordinary part of their lives. The two often went camping and noticed that coffee brewed outdoors, particularly in hot and humid conditions, could taste remarkably different from the same coffee made at home.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Tan Shing Win was coached by Keith Koay (first from right), a three-time Malaysian Barista Champion. — Picture courtesy of Tan Shing Win
“That observation sparked our curiosity. We wanted to understand why, and whether we could find an explanation through research and experimentation,” Keith says.
Shing Win’s competition routine also had to translate that curiosity into a compelling coffee experience. One challenge was showcasing the delicate character of a washed Geisha in a milk beverage.
Rather than selecting different coffees for each course, as competitors commonly do to maximise the potential of individual drinks, the team chose to use the same coffee across all three.
“We wanted to preserve the coffee’s identity while creating enough intensity for its flavours to shine through the milk,” Shing Win says.
They explored how moisture within the beans could help achieve that without changing the roast profile.
“It reminded me that sometimes, improving a cup isn’t about changing the coffee itself, but understanding how to work with what the coffee already has to offer.”
For Keith, that process was not separate from their everyday work.
“Much of what we presented on stage reflects what we quietly practise behind the bar every day,” he says. “It’s not necessarily something loud or visually spectacular.”
Behind the simplicity, Keith points to “a lot of observation, questioning, experimentation and attention to detail”, which are habits that support their philosophy of making tasty coffee.
What mattered to him was that Shing Win had brought this everyday approach onto the world stage and demonstrated that it belonged there.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Tan Shing Win has been supported throughout his preparation, ever since he won the Malaysia Barista Championship last year. — Picture courtesy of Tan Shing Win

Naturally, second place brought mixed emotions to Shing Win. He was happy, shocked and proud to finish runner-up in his debut at the championship, but the knowledge that first place was within reach made the moment bittersweet.
However, this historic result only fully sank in after he returned to Malaysia.

Shing Win says that his achievement was also the product of everyone who had supported him throughout the preparation, ever since he won the Malaysia Barista Championship last year: “My coach, mentor and team believed in me even before I believed in myself.”
He also received encouragement from the international coffee community, whose generosity moved him deeply.
“I think the biggest lesson I’ve learned is to be more selfless. So many people have shared their knowledge, experience and time with me without expecting anything in return.”
Shing Win’s milestone achievement has struck a chord across the Malaysian coffee community, many of whom are his peers, supporters, mentors and comrades in arms.
Jason Loo, who finished fourth at the 2025 World Barista Championship after winning the Malaysia Barista Championship four times, has been cheering him on.

“Seeing Shing Win follow that with a second-place finish reinforces the belief that our success is not a one-off achievement. We are building the foundation, the experience, and the confidence to compete consistently at this level,” Jason says.
He believes the country should also reconsider how it sees its place in the global coffee scene.
“We should no longer see ourselves as a small coffee nation trying to catch up. We have our own identity, talent, culture, and stories to bring to the world.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Tan Shing Win’s triumph at the WBC will inspire the next generation of Malaysian baristas. — Picture courtesy of Tan Shing Win

That shift might depend on an ecosystem the competitors find themselves in. Chiam Tow Jin — president of the Malaysia Specialty Coffee Association, co-founder of The Roast Things and the 2025 Malaysia Cup Tasters Champion — feels the achievement reflects both individual commitment and the wider industry that has developed around baristas.

He says, “Behind them are companies and teams willing to invest time, resources, and belief in their development. Equally important are the customers whose appreciation for good coffee makes it commercially sustainable for businesses to keep investing in their people.”

Competition also has value beyond the podium. According to Surender Kumar (or Suren), the 2023 Malaysia Barista Champion and co-founder of Ruits Juices: “It develops discipline, attention to detail and a better understanding of how to communicate what you do,” he says.

Suren hopes younger baristas will be empowered by Shing Win’s story to take their craft seriously and consider the different ways they can contribute, whether through competing, teaching, coaching or building businesses.
To these aspiring baristas, Keith’s advice is straightforward: find a good team, work hard, stay curious and “pray for a little luck”.

Shing Win agrees, adding that his next step is “to do the same for others. To share what I’ve learned, offer support wherever I can, and pass on the same positive energy that so many people have given me throughout this journey.”
No doubt his triumph at the WBC will inspire the next generation of Malaysian baristas, but the challenge now is to make that level of performance less of an exception and more of a standard.
Together, we can build a coffee culture in which more Malaysians have the knowledge, support and resources to compete on the world stage.
For more food fables and café chronicles, visit Life for Beginners.
5f2adefd940411af: PARIS: Some 2,800 troops from 10 European countries will this month stage in Poland the first exercise of a new multinational force in support of Ukraine, London and Paris said on Tuesday.

Led by France and the UK, the Multinational Force – Ukraine (MNF-U) has no offensive mission and is only to be deployed once a ceasefire is agreed to end the war sparked by Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
The force, which was set up in 2025 and already has an operational headquarters in Paris, is not a Nato operation and has little US involvement.
It aims to support the Ukrainian armed forces, ensure security in Ukrainian skies and allow economic activity to resume in the Black Sea.
But the extent and duration of the exercise, dubbed Koalicja ("Coalition" in Polish), risks antagonising Russia, with Moscow still showing little appetite to settle for peace.

"The exercise will allow the testing of the speed and efficiency at which several nations can deploy forces on land, sea and air to support Ukraine once hostilities have finished," said the joint statement released by the French defence ministry.
"This isn't a hypothetical plan, it's a real force, ready to help Ukraine once the fighting stops," UK Defence Minister Wes Streeting was quoted as saying in the UK statement.
The exercise is scheduled to last from Nov 9 to 22 in southeast Poland, not far from the Ukrainian border, involving 2,800 troops.
The largest contingent of 1,100 troops will come from France, with the UK deploying 300 soldiers.
Light equipment deployed

The first exercise for the coalition force is "a key milestone, as it will serve as a concrete demonstration of the MNF-U's ability to be deployed as soon as hostilities have ended," said French General Armel Dirou, who will co-lead the exercise alongside Britain's Lieutenant General Tom Bateman.

It will involve troops from Belgium, Estonia, Germany, France, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Poland, Spain, Sweden and the UK in air and land operations around the town of Nowa Deba, some 100km (62 miles) west of the Ukrainian border, the joint statement said.

Meanwhile, a maritime simulation will be led by Turkey from Istanbul to test preparedness for eventual mine-clearing operations in the Black Sea. Turkish troops will not be involved in the land exercise in Poland, it added.
Bateman emphasised that the force is not a "peacekeeping or ceasefire monitoring mission".

"It is not designed for offensive operations. Its purpose is to provide reassurance and support the regeneration of Ukraine's armed forces, strengthening their ability to deter and, if necessary, defend against future Russian aggression," he said.

Nevertheless, Moscow will be watching closely as the war – which has now lasted longer than World War I – grinds towards its five-year milestone with neither side apparently close to a decisive breakthrough.
Dirou said that the aim of the exercise was to prepare how the mission would be deployed, overcoming the various potential logistical and cultural issues between the different countries' militaries.
"This is not a show of force. We are not going to flex our muscles," he said.
It is expected that only light equipment, such as drones, will be deployed in Poland for anti-drone and self-defence exercises, rather than heavy weaponry, and that no tanks will be deployed.

Aspects tested in the exercise will include coordination arrangements, rehearsing the movement of personnel, equipment and supplies, and assessing whether the different components can integrate and operate effectively as one multinational force, said Bateman.

A representative for Disney declined to comment.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Oct 1 that Disney was planning a restructuring of its TV division, and cuts at the company’s legal and global affairs unit.

Other entertainment companies including Netflix, Sony Pictures Entertainment and Skydance’s Paramount and Warner Bros. divisions have also cut jobs as revenue from traditional television declines and streaming subscriber growth slows.
The also have to cope with more viewers tuning to social media, online videos and streaming services backed by tech giants like Amazon.com and Apple.

At the Bloomberg Screentime conference in Los Angeles last month, Disney president Dana Walden said that “there is a need to constantly evaluate how you’re structured and how big is the organisation. Technology set their sights on our business and we must survive and thrive and grow, and that’s what we’re going to do.”

5fe9edcda6a1e9df: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The government is finalising the draft Children (Amendment) Bill 2026 for submission to the Cabinet for consideration, said Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M Kulasegaran.

He said the amendments aimed to improve Section 97 of the Child Act 2001 (Act 611) following the abolition of mandatory death sentences and life imprisonment in 2023 and seek to establish a more proportionate sentencing approach and eliminate indefinite imprisonment of juvenile offenders without a specified detention period.

Kulasegaran said that under the existing Subsection 97(2) of Act 611, the court must order a child offender to be detained in prison at the pleasure of the King or the State Ruler, as applicable under the relevant laws, without specifying a maximum detention period.

“The Madani Government is committed to improving this legal framework to ensure a clearer and more proportionate sentencing approach that takes into account the principles of justice for children as well as public safety,” he said when winding up the debate on the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 at the committee stage for the Prime Minister’s Department in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.

He said a Special Committee to Review and Amend Section 97 of Act 611 had been established to examine proposed improvements to the provision, taking into account the principles of the best interests of the child, rehabilitation and reintegration, as well as international best practices.
Kulasegaran said the findings of the review had led to the Cabinet’s agreement on Sept 30 to four policy decisions concerning the proposed amendments to Section 97 of Act 611.
He said the proposed policy decisions were subsequently presented to the Conference of Rulers on Oct 14 for consideration and deliberation.

Meanwhile, on the proposal to establish a Law Drafting Unit in Parliament, Kulasegaran said the move was progressive and in line with efforts to strengthen the independence and autonomy of the country’s legislative institution.

“This matter merits consideration within the framework of implementing the Parliamentary Services Act 2025, subject to deliberation by the Parliamentary Service Council and the relevant staffing and legal requirements,” he said.

He said the establishment of the unit would enable Parliament to develop its own legislative drafting expertise, particularly to assist Members of Parliament in preparing Private Members’ Bills and proposed amendments to legislation without having to rely entirely on the drafting expertise of the Executive. — Bernama
7dad61a7c982802b: KUALA LUMPUR: The inquest into the shooting in Durian Tunggal, Melaka, on Nov 24 last year, which claimed the lives of three men, was not deliberately delayed.
The scheduling of the proceedings is subject to the court's processes and case management.

Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) decided on July 20, 2026, that an inquest should be held after reviewing the investigation papers and all evidence submitted by the police.

He said the decision followed a thorough investigation by the police into the incident. This included reviewing the evidence gathered and complying with further instructions and requirements set by the AGC.
He said police's Criminal Investigation Department at Bukit Aman had filed an application with the Melaka court on Aug 11 for a date to be set for the inquest.
The police are still waiting for the court to determine the date.
"In this regard, the scheduling of the proceedings is subject to the court's processes and case management.
"The government wishes to stress that the inquest proceedings have not been deliberately delayed.

"The decision to hold an inquest was made following a comprehensive investigation, including a review of the evidence gathered and compliance with further instructions and requirements from the A-GC," he said in a written reply published on the parliament website.
He was responding to RSN Rayer (PH-Jelutong), who asked the home minister when the inquest into the shooting in Durian Tunggal was expected to begin and the reasons for the delay.
Saifuddin said the Home Ministry guaranteed that the police would extend full cooperation to the court and A-GC in conducting the inquest.
He said the government respected the independence of the judicial process and would not pre-empt any court findings.
"The inquest is important to establish the cause and actual circumstances of the deaths through a transparent, fair and lawful process," he said.
The inquest will be conducted under Section 339(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code (Act 593).
In the incident, three men aged between 24 and 29 were shot dead after one of them allegedly swung a parang at a police corporal at an oil palm plantation in Durian Tunggal at 4am.
The incident left the police personnel, who was in his early 30s, with serious injuries to his left hand.

89f9d57fa8194c5c: NEWCASTLE, Nov 3 — Everton increased the pressure on under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle as Thierno Barry sealed a 1-0 win at St James’ Park on Monday.
Barry netted early in the second half to lift Everton into seventh place in the Premier League and leave Newcastle languishing in 13th.
Newcastle midfielder Jacob Ramsey was sent off in the final seconds for a crude foul on Harrison Armstrong.
It was a fitting end to another painful defeat for Saudi-funded Newcastle, who have lost four of their past five matches in all competitions, winning just twice in their last seven.
Jaissle and his players were booed off at half-time and again after the final whistle as the German coach begins to feel the heat in his first season in charge.
Hired following Eddie Howe’s surprise close-season exit, former Red Bull Salzburg and Al-Ahli boss Jaissle has struggled to make an impact on Tyneside.
Jaissle desperately needs a win at fellow strugglers Fulham on Saturday to ease the mounting scrutiny.
Bizarrely, Newcastle have lost 22 of their last 33 Premier League matches on a Monday and many of their supporters headed for the exits well before the final whistle on a miserable rainy night.

Barry’s eighth goal this season, including four in his last six matches, gave Everton their second win against Newcastle in the space of five days following their 3-1 victory in the League Cup fourth round on Thursday.
Everton ended their run of two successive league defeats after losing against Arsenal and Chelsea.
It was Everton’s first away league win since February 28 when they took three points on their previous visit to Newcastle.
Jack Grealish was absent from the Everton squad for a second successive game after being axed for the Newcastle match last week due to a “breach of club discipline”.
Ramsey sees red
The on-loan Manchester City winger, who has been criticised for his off-field behaviour for much of his colourful career, reportedly skipped training prior to the League Cup clash.
Everton said he was “not match fit” for the rematch with the Magpies, but his team coped just fine without him.
Newcastle made a lively start and went close when Harvey Barnes fired just wide before Joelinton was narrowly off target from 25 yards.
But chances were at a premium for both sides in a scrappy first half more notable for perspiration than inspiration.
Everton’s opener four minutes after half-time was in keeping with the grimy fare that preceded it.
Newcastle’s dismal marking let in Tyrique George for a shot that drew a weak save from Lukas Hornicek.
Hornicek could only push it straight into the path of Barry for a simple tap-in that survived a lengthy VAR check for offside.
It was a chance so easy that even the notoriously erratic Barry couldn’t fail to hit the target, although Newcastle were aggrieved by the VAR decision to let it stand.
Fabian Schar wasted a good opportunity to equalise when he blazed wide.
And Jaissle’s men came within a whisker of levelling through Anthony Elanga, whose close-range shot clipped the post and rolled along the goalline before Everton scrambled it clear.
Summing up their inconsistent display, it took 86 minutes for Newcastle to finally register a shot on target and even then Yoane Wissa’s effort was routine for Pickford.
Wissa did manage to force a better save from Pickford in stoppage time.
But Ramsey saw red for two bookings in the space of 60 seconds to complete Newcastle’s misery. — AFP
c29f44ceb19aeec1: WASHINGTON, Nov 3 — US President Donald Trump on Monday signaled progress in talks with Iran to avoid a return to war, as Tehran said “intensive” exchanges were underway while offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions.
A deal with Tehran “could happen,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform, a day before crucial US midterm elections. He added that “Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible.”
Vice President JD Vance separately said that both he and Trump were optimistic about securing an agreement.
“We’ve certainly made some progress. We’ll see if we can make some more,” Vance told reporters on Monday.
Oil prices, sent rocketing by Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz energy corridor, plunged by more than seven percent on Monday on optimism over a possible end to the eight-month-old conflict.
Trump also pointed to tumbling oil prices on his social media post.

The renewed diplomatic signals come ahead of Tuesday’s midterms, in which Trump’s Republican Party is pushing to retain control of Congress despite voter dissatisfaction over the war and higher fuel prices.
Democrats expect to win at least partial control of Congress and impose political constraints on Trump for the first time in two years.
Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Monday that indirect talks with Washington were taking place via mediators.
“Given the sensitivity and gravity of the current situation, consultations and deliberations are very intensive,” Araghchi said in a video interview with the official IRNA news agency.
“Qatar and Pakistan are playing a very active mediating role in these negotiations.”
China also urged a return to negotiations, while Iran’s security chief discussed the conflict with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Earlier, the Axios news outlet reported that Vance had sent a letter to Iranian national security chief Mohsen Rezaei about possible new talks, marking the highest-level move in months.
Iran’s First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref said the messages received from the US were “an acknowledgement of our victory.”
But Trump had previously kept up his threats against Iran, telling a campaign rally that at “some point we’re going to have to give them the hammer.”
‘Good-faith approach’
A senior Iranian official said Tehran was ready to open Strait of Hormuz, an export conduit for the energy-rich Gulf, within two days — as long as Washington agrees to its list of demands.

In September, Iran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen the strait if the US agreed to demands including ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
“The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran’s good-faith approach,” foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told reporters at a briefing.

Chinese President Xi Jinping also discussed the war with Oman’s Sultan Haitham bin Tariq in Beijing on Monday — the first visit to China by the Gulf nation’s head of state since diplomatic ties were established.

“The two sides called for resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, urging the United States and Iran to pursue a peaceful path, achieve a ceasefire (and) prevent war entirely,” an Omani statement said.
‘No compromises’
China held meetings with Iranian and Saudi officials in Beijing on Monday as well.

Beijing supports Tehran in “safeguarding its own sovereignty and security,” Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Ali Bagheri, deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, according to a Chinese statement.

Bagheri told Wang that “Tehran’s stance on defending its national security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity remains unchanged, and that Iran will make no compromises in this regard,” state TV reported.
In an interview with Al Jazeera released Sunday, Araghchi said Washington must accept a new route agreed between Iran and Oman for transiting the strait.
He said the US must also remove sanctions imposed recently and reduce American troop numbers in the region.
On Saturday, Trump said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets including Pickaxe mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility.
Baqaei warned that any act of aggression against Iran “will be met with a powerful, immediate and comprehensive response.” — AFP

401834a52e8b2ef8: WASHINGTON, Nov 3 — The US Supreme Court on Monday rejected a Trump administration emergency bid to force California to set aside the mail-in ballots of more than 20,000 people on the grounds they may not be American citizens.

Acting a day before the US midterm elections, the top court denied the request in an unsigned, one-sentence ruling, as is common in urgent cases before the court. It gave no reasoning for the decision.

The federal government had accused California of having 190,000 illegal voters on its rolls. It recently revised the figure to 20,000 and filed an emergency lawsuit — after early voting had begun — to stop the state from sending ballots to them.
The Supreme Court action came after lower courts last week — and again on Monday — rejected the demand by the Department of Justice (DOJ), with one judge calling it brazen pre-election interference.

Solicitor General D. John Sauer, in an emergency filing with the Supreme Court, had said that “once California commingles the challenged ballots with lawful ones, there is no way to get the challenged ballots back.”

The California ballot case appeared to be another attempt by the administration to cast doubt on the results of Tuesday’s vote, in which President Donald Trump’s Republican Party is at risk of losing control of Congress.
Trump — who has never acknowledged his own election defeat by Democrat Joe Biden in 2020 — has been claiming for months that there will be fraud in the midterms.
US District Judge David Carter last week refused to order the seizure of the ballots and sided with the government of Democratic-led California.
“The DOJ’s actions are indicative of a broad, ongoing pattern of attempted election interference by federal officials,” Carter said.
Another district judge, James Boasberg, also ruled against the Trump administration on Monday, saying the lists of alleged non-citizens were “flawed.”

A controversy similar to California’s arose in neighbouring Nevada. The administration said initially it had identified 16,000 non-citizen voters there, but after verification procedures that number dropped to 185 — and then to zero.
Studies repeatedly show that while cases of voter fraud exist, such incidents are extremely rare and do not influence election results.

In another closely-watched election case, a federal judge in Alaska over the weekend tossed out a bid by the Trump administration to hold up US Senate election results in the state should the Democratic candidate win.

The DOJ had asked the court to block certification of the results if Republican Dan Sullivan, the incumbent, loses on Tuesday because a second candidate also named Dan Sullivan would have siphoned off votes.

Mary Peltola, the Democratic candidate for Senate in Alaska, has denied recruiting the second Sullivan into the race, but The New York Times reported that members of her campaign staff had been involved. — AFP
