Anwar yang juga menteri kewangan berkata Putrajaya dan kerajaan Sabah turut berusaha memuktamadkan formula tetap bagi menentukan jumlah yang menjadi hak negeri itu daripada hasil Persekutuan seperti diperuntukkan dalam Perlembagaan.
Ketika membentangkan Belanjawan 2027 di Dewan Rakyat, Anwar mengakui bayaran geran khas kepada Sabah selama beberapa dekad tidak meningkat seiring keperluan pembangunan negeri itu.
“Kerajaan Madani telah menaikkannya sebanyak tiga kali,” katanya merujuk bayaran geran khas RM300 juta pada 2023 dan RM600 juta pada 2025.
“Kadar interim terkini ialah RM1.5 bilion dan akan dibayar sepenuhnya sebelum akhir tahun.
“Rundingan dengan Sabah dan Sarawak diteruskan bagi mendapatkan formula tahunan yang adil dan mampan,” katanya.
FMT meneliti apakah sebenarnya geran khas 40% itu, kepentingan bayaran RM1.5 bilion dan beberapa isu yang masih perlu diselesaikan.
Apakah geran khas 40%?
Perjanjian Malaysia 1963 (MA63) ditandatangani kerajaan United Kingdom, Persekutuan Tanah Melayu, Borneo Utara yang kini dikenali sebagai Sabah, Sarawak dan Singapura bagi membentuk Malaysia.

Perjanjian itu menetapkan aturan perlembagaan, kewangan dan pentadbiran bagi persekutuan baharu, termasuk beberapa perlindungan untuk Sabah dan Sarawak yang kemudian dimasukkan ke dalam Perlembagaan Persekutuan.
Antara perlindungan itu ialah geran khas 40% yang diperuntukkan menerusi Seksyen 2(1), Bahagian IV, Jadual Kesepuluh Perlembagaan Persekutuan.
Peguam Mazlianie Mohd Lan menyifatkannya sebagai hak di bawah Perlembagaan yang memberikan Sabah 40% daripada pertambahan hasil bersih yang dikutip kerajaan Persekutuan dari negeri itu.
Tempoh tanpa semakan
Mengikut Perkara 112D Perlembagaan Persekutuan, geran khas itu perlu dikaji semula setiap lima tahun oleh kerajaan Persekutuan dan kerajaan negeri.

Bagaimanapun, tiada kajian semula dibuat antara 1974 hingga 2021, satu tempoh yang digelar sebagai 'lost years' atau tahun-tahun terlepas. Sebaliknya, Sabah hanya menerima bayaran tetap RM26.7 juta setahun.

Pada 17 Okt 2025, Mahkamah Tinggi Kota Kinabalu memutuskan dalam prosiding semakan kehakiman yang difailkan Sabah Law Society bahawa kerajaan Persekutuan gagal melaksanakan tanggungjawab perlembagaannya kepada Sabah kerana tidak menjalankan kajian berkala sepanjang tempoh berkenaan.

Hakim Celestina Stuel Galid mengarahkan kerajaan Persekutuan dan Sabah mengadakan rundingan secara terus bagi memuktamadkan jumlah yang perlu dibayar kepada Sabah untuk tempoh itu, dengan bayaran dibuat dalam tempoh 180 hari daripada tarikh penghakiman.
Bagaimanapun, perintah itu ditangguhkan Mahkamah Rayuan sementara menunggu keputusan rayuan Putrajaya. Rayuan berkenaan didengar pada 29 Okt lalu dan keputusan masih belum dibuat.
Sementara itu, Sabah menerima RM53.4 juta pada 2020 sebelum jumlah itu kembali kepada RM26.7 juta pada tahun berikutnya.
Pada 2022, satu perintah kajian semula menetapkan bayaran yang meningkat secara berperingkat, bermula RM125.6 juta.
Geran interim itu kemudian dinaikkan kepada RM300 juta pada 2023, RM600 juta pada 2025 dan RM1.5 bilion tahun ini.
Mengapa RM1.5 bilion penting?
Anwar dan Ketua Menteri Sabah Hajiji Noor menyifatkan peruntukan tahun ini, jumlah tertinggi setakat ini, sebagai bukti komitmen untuk memuktamadkan mekanisme pengiraan geran khas tersebut.
Mazlianie berkata reaksi orang ramai terhadap bayaran itu bercampur.
Ada yang menganggapnya tidak mencukupi dan sekadar penyelesaian sementara, manakala sebahagian lagi melihatnya sebagai tanda kesediaan kerajaan memenuhi hak rakyat Sabah di bawah Perlembagaan.
“Bayaran interim RM1.5 bilion itu harus dilihat secara positif.

“Bagaimanapun, ia tidak boleh mengalihkan perhatian daripada matlamat utama untuk menentukan, tanpa berlengah lagi, jumlah penuh geran khas 40% yang menjadi hak Sabah di bawah Perlembagaan Persekutuan, termasuk bagi tahun-tahun yang terlepas dan tahun selepasnya,” katanya.
Bagaimana untuk muktamadkan formula?
Menurut Mazlianie, beberapa isu perundangan, teknikal dan perakaunan yang rumit perlu diselesaikan sebelum formula tetap dan praktikal bagi mengira geran khas 40% Sabah dapat dimuktamadkan.
Antaranya ialah takrif 'hasil bersih', iaitu hasil yang terakru kepada Persekutuan selepas ditolak serahan statutori yang diterima negeri.

Katanya, kedua-dua pihak juga perlu menentukan sama ada hasil Persekutuan yang diperoleh di Sabah daripada perkara di bawah Senarai Persekutuan, seperti pelancongan, minyak, medan minyak, Cukai Keuntungan Harta Tanah dan cukai lain, perlu dimasukkan dalam pengiraan.
Ini kerana hasil tersebut menjadi sebahagian daripada Kumpulan Wang Disatukan Persekutuan.
Satu lagi persoalan yang perlu diperjelaskan ialah apakah yang dikira sebagai 'potongan yang dibenarkan'.
Selain itu, perlu ditentukan sama ada hasil yang diperoleh 'dari Sabah' hanya merangkumi kawasan daratan atau turut meliputi perairan wilayah, pelantar benua dan Zon Ekonomi Eksklusif (ZEE).
Menurut Mazlianie, perkara itu menunjukkan keperluan untuk menetapkan dengan jelas sempadan dan skop wilayah yang perlu diambil kira dalam pengiraan.
Satu lagi isu ialah kaedah penyediaan akaun kewangan.
Mazlianie berkata antara 1964 hingga 1972, Kementerian Kewangan menerbitkan anggaran hasil dan perbelanjaan Persekutuan dengan pecahan berasingan bagi Semenanjung Malaysia, Sabah dan Sarawak.
Bagaimanapun, sejak 1973, akaun Persekutuan menggabungkan angka berkenaan sebagai jumlah keseluruhan negara.
“Penerbitan laporan kewangan yang telus dan mengasingkan hasil yang diperoleh dari Sabah amat penting bagi membolehkan formula 40% dikira dengan tepat,” katanya.
Adakah Putrajaya berada di landasan betul?

Mazlianie berkata kerajaan Persekutuan dilihat bergerak ke arah yang betul menerusi beberapa langkah, termasuk penubuhan Majlis Tindakan Pelaksanaan Perjanjian Malaysia 1963 (MTPMA63), papan pemuka MA63, peningkatan bayaran interim dan rundingan berterusan antara Putrajaya dan Sabah.
Menurutnya, perkembangan terkini menunjukkan peningkatan ketara berbanding tahun-tahun sebelumnya apabila isu berkaitan MA63 kurang mendapat perhatian dalam perbincangan awam.
Bagaimanapun, katanya, usaha berkenaan tidak mengurangkan tanggungjawab kerajaan untuk menunaikan hak Sabah terhadap geran khas 40% seperti diperuntukkan dalam Perlembagaan.
“Perkara ini tidak boleh terus dilengahkan. Keperluan pembangunan Sabah perlu ditangani segera dan hak perlembagaannya terhadap bayaran tahunan 40% mesti ditunaikan tanpa kelewatan lanjut,” katanya.
Mazlianie turut menggesa ketelusan lebih menyeluruh dalam papan pemuka MA63.

Katanya, ia perlu menyediakan perkembangan lebih terperinci bagi setiap isu yang masih belum diselesaikan, membuka ruang kepada penglibatan awam yang bermakna serta menyatakan pihak yang bertanggungjawab terhadap setiap perkara bagi meningkatkan akauntabiliti.
Di sebalik aspek perundangan dan perlembagaan, beliau berkata rakyat Malaysia perlu melihat geran khas 40% itu sebagai pelaburan dalam pertumbuhan negara dan bukannya beban kewangan.

Menurutnya, pembayaran hak itu secara konsisten dapat mempercepat pembangunan Sabah, mengukuhkan sektor utama seperti pertanian, pelancongan dan industri berasaskan sumber secara mampan, sekali gus meningkatkan hasil negara.
“Geran khas 40% tidak seharusnya dilihat sebagai perbelanjaan yang menghakis kekayaan negara.
“Ekonomi Sabah yang lebih kukuh juga akan mengukuhkan ekonomi Malaysia,” katanya.
cae2efd0f283f0f1: PETALING JAYA: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced on Oct 7 that Sabah would receive an interim special grant of RM1.5 billion this year.

Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said Putrajaya and the Sabah government were also working towards a permanent formula for calculating the state’s entitlement to its share of federal revenue, as provided for in the Federal Constitution.
Tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat, the prime minister acknowledged that the special grant payments to Sabah had “for decades” failed to keep pace with the state’s development needs.
“The Madani government has raised it on three occasions,” he said, referring to special grant payments of RM300 million in 2023 and RM600 million in 2025.

“The latest interim rate stands at RM1.5 billion, to be paid in full before the year is out. Negotiations with Sabah and Sarawak continue towards a fair and sustainable annual formula,” the prime minister added.
FMT looks into what the 40% special grant entails, the significance of the latest RM1.5 billion figure, and some of the challenges faced.
What is the 40% special grant?

The Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) is the treaty signed by the governments of the United Kingdom, the Federation of Malaya, North Borneo (now Sabah), Sarawak and Singapore that led to the formation of Malaysia.

It sets out the constitutional, financial and administrative arrangements governing the new federation, including various safeguards for Sabah and Sarawak, which were subsequently incorporated into the constitution.
One of those safeguards was the 40% special grant, enshrined in Section 2(1) of Part IV of the Tenth Schedule to the constitution.
Lawyer Mazlianie Mohd Lan described the grant as “a constitutional entitlement that gives Sabah 40% of the growth in net revenue collected by the federal government from the state”.
‘Lost years’

Under Article 112D of the Federal Constitution, the special grant was subject to a five-yearly review by the federal and state governments. However, no review took place between 1974 and 2021, dubbed the “lost years”. Instead, a fixed sum of RM26.7 million was paid annually.

On Oct 17 last year, the Kota Kinabalu High Court ruled, in judicial review proceedings brought by the Sabah Law Society, that the federal government had breached its constitutional duties to Sabah by failing to conduct periodic reviews over the lost years.

Justice Celestina Stuel Galid ordered the two governments to enter into direct negotiations to finalise the quantum due to Sabah over the lost years, and for payment to be made within 180 days of the judgment.
The order has been stayed by the Court of Appeal pending disposal of Putrajaya’s appeal, which was heard on Oct 29 and is awaiting a decision.
Meanwhile, in 2020, Sabah received RM53.4 million, although the sum reverted to RM26.7 million the following year.

In 2022, a review order introduced escalating payments starting at RM125.6 million. The following year, the interim grant was revised to RM300 million, before the federal government raised it to RM600 million in 2025, and RM1.5 billion this year.
Why the RM1.5 billion allocation matters

Both Anwar and Sabah chief minister Hajiji Noor have hailed this year’s allocation, by far the highest financial quantum ever delivered, as a demonstration of genuine commitment towards finalising the mechanism for computation of the special grant.

According to Mazlianie, the general view of the public has been mixed, with some calling it “insufficient” and “only a temporary fix”, while others have welcomed it as a display of a desire to fulfil the constitutional rights of Sabahans.
“The RM1.5 billion interim payment should be viewed positively,” said Mazlianie.

“However, it must not distract from the ultimate objective of determining, without further delay, Sabah’s full 40% special grant entitlement under the Federal Constitution, including for the ‘lost’ and subsequent years.”
What is needed to finalise the formula?
According to Mazlianie, several complex legal, technical and accounting issues must be resolved to arrive at a permanent and workable formula for calculating Sabah’s 40% special grant.
For instance, “net revenue” is defined as revenue that accrues to the federation less statutory assignments received by the state.

Mazlianie said the parties must also determine whether federal earnings in Sabah derived from items under the constitution's federal list — such as tourism, oil, oilfields, real property gains tax and other taxes — should be included in the calculation, given that such revenue forms part of the Federal Consolidated Fund.
She said another issue that must be resolved is what constitutes a “permissible deduction”.
Likewise, questions arise as to whether revenue derived “from Sabah” covers only the landmass or also extends to its territorial waters, the continental shelf and the exclusive economic zone.
This, she said, underscores the need to establish the parameters of territorial sovereignty.
Another matter that would need to be addressed is the manner in which the financial accounts are kept.

According to Mazlianie, between 1964 and 1972, the finance ministry published federal revenue and expenditure estimates with distinct columns separating revenue from Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
However, she said that since 1973, federal accounts have consolidated the numbers into aggregate national sums.
“Publishing transparent, segregated financial reports isolating Sabah's derived revenue is essential to calculate the 40% formula accurately,” she said.
Is Putrajaya moving in the right direction?

Mazlianie said the federal government appeared to be moving in the right direction, pointing to initiatives such as the MA63 Implementation Action Council, the MA63 dashboard, increased interim payments and continued engagement between Putrajaya and Sabah.
She described the recent developments as a marked improvement from earlier years, when discussions on MA63 issues were far less prominent in public discourse.
However, she stressed that these efforts did not diminish the government's obligation to fulfil Sabah's constitutional entitlement to the 40% special grant.
“Time is of the essence. Sabah's development needs must be addressed urgently and the constitutional right to the annual 40% entitlement must be fulfilled without further delay,” she said.

Mazlianie also called for greater transparency in the MA63 dashboard, saying it should provide more detailed updates on the status of each outstanding issue, allow for meaningful public engagement, and identify the individuals responsible for specific matters to promote accountability and ownership.
Beyond the legal and constitutional aspects, she said Malaysians should view the 40% special grant as an investment in national growth rather than a financial burden.

According to her, consistent payment of the entitlement would help accelerate Sabah's development, strengthen key sectors such as agriculture, tourism and sustainable resource-based industries, and ultimately contribute to higher national revenue.
“The 40% special grant should not be seen as an expense that depletes the nation's wealth. A stronger Sabah economy will also strengthen Malaysia's economy,” she said.
3e18cf734299dcc5: PETALING JAYA: Forgetfulness, difficulty concentrating and mental fatigue are often brushed aside as an unavoidable part of getting older or juggling a busy lifestyle.
But as more people look for ways to support their brain health, one herbal remedy that has stood the test of time continues to attract attention: ginkgo biloba.
"Ginkgo biloba has maintained its enduring popularity because it is widely cultivated around the world, making it readily accessible," pharmacist Benjamin Lim told FMT Lifestyle.

“It acts as an antioxidant and helps support healthy blood circulation. Research also shows that it possesses anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties, which may contribute to maintaining brain health.”
Ginkgo biloba has a long and colourful history - its ancestors first appeared over 200 million years ago, during the Jurassic period.
According to fossil records, ginkgo-like trees once grew across much of the world, but most species disappeared during periods of mass extinction.

Ginkgo biloba is the only surviving species of its ancient lineage. The tree is believed to have thrived after being cultivated in China for centuries, with Buddhist monks said to have planted and protected ginkgo biloba around temples and monasteries.
While the first trees were introduced to Europe in the early 1700s and later to North America, ginkgo biloba has been used in traditional Chinese medicine for over 1,000 years.
It was first cherished as an ornamental plant due to its distinctive fan-shaped leaves. But interest as a medicinal plant grew rapidly during the 20th century, particularly in Germany and France.
Ginkgo biloba is also renowned for its extraordinary resilience. Case in point: six trees growing within about 2km of the epicentre of the Hiroshima atomic bomb blast in 1945 survived the explosion.
Against all odds, the hardy trees produced new shoots in the months that followed - and are still alive over 80 years later.
Health benefits

According to Lim, ginkgo biloba contains ginkgo flavonoid glycosides, potent antioxidants that help neutralise free radicals. By reducing oxidative stress, these compounds help protect cells from damage associated with ageing and chronic disease.
The tree’s leaves also contain terpene lactones, a group of unique bioactive compounds that support healthy blood circulation and help protect nerve cells.
Ginkgo biloba is the only known natural source of ginkgolides, a rare class of active compounds extensively studied for their anti-inflammatory, neuroprotective and cardiovascular properties.

"By increasing nitric oxide levels, ginkgo biloba helps keep blood vessels healthy and responsive, promoting better blood flow. It also inhibits the platelet-activating factor, a compound involved in blood clotting, which may further improve circulation," Lim said.

The elderly, in particular, report the most benefits as they are most prone to issues with blood circulation and cognitive decline. Nevertheless, Lim believes people of any age group can benefit from taking the product.

"Anyone who experiences frequent stress, or whose work or lifestyle depends on staying mentally sharp and focused, may benefit. However, it is not a supplement that produces immediate results: its benefits build gradually with consistent, long-term use," Lim pointed out.
He also noted that ginkgo biloba should be viewed as a complement to, rather than a substitute for, a healthy lifestyle, and is most effective when combined with a balanced diet and regular exercise.
When choosing a ginkgo biloba supplement, Lim advises consumers to consider three key factors.

The first is standardisation. A high-quality product should contain a standardised extract with 24% ginkgo flavonoid glycosides and 6% terpene lactones, the benchmark formulation used in most clinical studies.
Secondly, consumers should check whether the product contains leaf extract or only powdered ginkgo leaves.
Standardised extracts are produced by concentrating the plant's beneficial compounds, resulting in more consistent levels of the active ingredients than powdered leaf products.
Finally, Lim stressed the importance of carefully reading the label to determine the amount of ginkgo biloba extract in each tablet.
“If you can, try to find out what kind of testing was done on the product, and whether the brand is known to be reliable,” he concluded.
02bb090fcc778bc1: TUMPAT, Nov 3 — The Southeast Brigade of the General Operations Force (GOF) recorded 1,493 cross-border crime cases between Jan 1 and Nov 1, with enforcement operations resulting in 1,733 arrests and seizures worth more than RM82.56 million.

Its commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the achievement demonstrated his personnel’s dedication and efficiency in carrying out enforcement duties aimed at safeguarding national security and sovereignty.

He said GOF had strengthened its intelligence capabilities and heightened personnel awareness of emerging threats, particularly the use of alternative routes and hidden locations by cross-border criminals seeking to evade detection.

“We cannot rely solely on conventional approaches or wait for threats to emerge before taking action. We must stay one step ahead by identifying changes in their patterns and modus operandi,” he told reporters after a handover of duties ceremony from the GOF 9th Battalion to the 7th Battalion for Ops Taring Wawasan Kelantan at the GOF Tactical Post in Pengkalan Kubor here yesterday.

Ahmad Radzi said each battalion must conduct assessments of its operational areas, identify high-risk locations and regularly update intelligence information to ensure operations focusing on prevention and risk assessment were carried out effectively.

On efforts to tackle illegal immigration, he said GOF operations went beyond making arrests to uncovering syndicate networks, those facilitating illegal crossings and individuals shielding the migrants’ movements from detection.
He said tackling the issue required a comprehensive and sustained preventive approach, including identifying high-risk areas, those involved and their modus operandi to curb such activities.
“As of yesterday, a total of 921 undocumented migrants of various nationalities had been detained, comprising 802 in Kelantan, 104 in Pahang and 15 in Terengganu,” he said. — Bernama
836a6ff71898661a: KYIV, Nov 3 — Ukraine said Monday that Russian strikes on a school distributing humanitarian aid killed at least 26 people, dashing fragile hopes of “progress toward peace” after a local ceasefire in the south expired without violations.

Russia resumed its strikes on the southern region of Kherson after the end of a ceasefire in the area, the longest truce in the war raging between the neighbours since Russia’s 2022 invasion, Kyiv said.

A rare pause in the fighting, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump to enable a mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, ended Sunday after starting on Tuesday, with neither side reporting breaches.
But hours after the truce, Russia targeted a village in Zaporizhzhia, adjacent to Kherson, with repeated strikes that killed at least 26 people, the acting regional governor said.
Some of the dead had come to collect aid at a local school.
Footage posted by the Ukrainian emergency services showed the building reduced to piles of smouldering rubble and rescuers working at the site.
“Every Monday, humanitarian aid was distributed to people there,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said in his daily address.
“The Russians carried out the first strike just as people arrived — several aerial bombs. Then, there was a repeat strike — more aerial bombs, this time targeting the shelter.”
Among those killed were “two rescue workers and four police officers”, acting regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said on Telegram.
The service named the rescuers as two 44-year-olds: Denys Konovalenko and Oleksy Sushchevsky.
“Every day, they went out to help people, working in dangerous conditions and risking their own lives to save others,” it said in a statement.
Zelensky said that after the Oleshky truce, “there was a moment when the next steps could have shown that progress toward peace was possible”.
“With these killings, Russia is sending an entirely opposite signal: Russia is counting on more killings. There must be a response to this.”
Russia fortifies positions
The ceasefire last week enabled an evacuation of the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.
It was the longest pause in fighting between the neighbours in the war, which is grinding through its fifth year after killing hundreds of thousands of people and displacing millions.
A senior Ukrainian figure told AFP on Sunday that Russia refused a Ukrainian offer to extend the truce.
Kyiv’s military also alleged that Moscow had used the pause in fighting to “fortify its positions”.
The Kremlin did not deny the accusations, with its spokesman Dmitry Peskov telling reporters Monday: “This is a completely normal practice in such situations.”
He alleged the Ukrainian army had also used pauses in fighting in the past to regroup.

Moscow saw the Oleshky humanitarian mission as “successful”, Peskov added, praising the “good cooperation between all sides” and singling out the role of its human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova.
Lantratova oversaw the ceasefire alongside her Ukrainian counterpart Dmytro Lubinets in one of the most substantial instances of Russian-Ukrainian cooperation since the start of the war.
The mission saw people evacuated to both Ukraine-controlled territory and Moscow-annexed Crimea.
The Kremlin said that no other similar missions were being planned “at the moment”.
US-led talks between Russia and Ukraine are set to resume next week, US special envoy Steve Witkoff said Monday.
President Donald Trump has pushed for a settlement to the dragging war but there has been no breakthrough.
The talks — to be held November 10 and 11 in Abu Dhabi, Witkoff said — come as Kyiv and its European allies worry that Trump has increasingly sided with Moscow.
Cyberattacks
Both Russia and Ukraine said overnight that their emergency warnings apps were hacked in apparent cyberattacks that came hours after the truce had ended.
Ukraine said it suspected its air raid alert system had been compromised, after false alerts of a radiation threat were sent to millions.
The warning system provides vital information about incoming Russian drones and missiles.
Russia has intensified its attacks this year, firing ballistic missiles and fast jet-powered drones, both of which are hard to intercept.
Moscow said that an app belonging to its emergency situations ministry that also warns of attacks had been hacked, too.
The app is not widely used in Russia, where warnings of Ukrainian drone attacks are not as common and typically sent by text message in border regions. — AFP
c265e7c697ef45ec: PARIS, Nov 3 — Cyberattacks affecting supermarket refrigeration systems in several European countries yesterday highlighted the risks associated with connecting industrial equipment to the internet.

After a previous attack in France in October, several chains in Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden experienced stark rises in fridge and freezer temperatures yesterday, forcing them to throw away spoilt produce.
Real world effects

Industrial equipment such as refrigeration systems, once operated largely offline, is now commonly connected to the internet so it can be monitored and managed remotely, cybersecurity specialists including Antoine Hautin, secretary-general of the Almond cybersecurity consultancy, told AFP.
That connectivity can also provide an avenue for attackers to interfere with physical systems through digital networks.
In France, the attackers targeted the fridge regulation system made by the Danish firm Danfoss, which is used by many shops.

“Most of the time, that’s done through a web interface. You connect to it with a password and you then have the possibility to choose what the temperature in the fridge is,” said Kevin Tellier, cybersecurity engineer at Synacktiv.

While these systems “are normally on a closed network” and “are not supposed to be accessible from the Internet”, a number of them ended up being exposed “to anyone with some basic knowledge”, he added.

Without proper protections, “any factory or equipment” connected to the internet — ranging from carmakers to electricity or transport infrastructure — could face similar risks, said Olivier Daloy, a cybersecurity expert at Zscaler.
How was it done?
According to another cyber expert who requested anonymity, industrial infrastructure is particularly vulnerable because it links IT systems with oft-outdated physical equipment.
By infiltrating those IT systems, hackers could hijack that infrastructure and cause disruption in the real world.
Daloy highlighted two particular risks: the exploitation of a technical vulnerability and the use of compromised credentials allowing hackers to log in to the equipment.
He pointed to the Stuxnet virus in 2010, which caused a series of failures in Iran’s centrifuge fleet used for uranium enrichment, as a past example.
In France, the October cyberattack was made possible by “basic security shortcomings”, according to Vincent Strubel, head of France’s National Cybersecurity Agency.
In particular, he blamed the fridges’ “direct exposure to the internet... without any particular security and with weak passwords”.
Who could be behind it?
Figuring out who could be behind the attack in France is “extremely complicated”, Daloy said.
Tellier agreed. “It could be anybody. The attack was not extremely sophisticated, so we cannot determine whether the hackers have significant resources or not.”
One security source told AFP that the investigation into the breach will “extend far after the event itself”.
A 2025 French national security document identified such attacks as “one of the threats that must be treated as a priority”.
“These incidents highlight how vulnerable food supply chains are to cyberattacks,” with far-reaching consequences, the document said. — AFP
6d4058b25c535956: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Traffic congestion in Bukit Jalil, particularly during concerts and large-scale events, has prompted the government to explore smart city solutions while refining traffic management plans to improve traffic flow in the area.

Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud had appointed consultants to conduct a Bukit Jalil micro-traffic management study, taking into account various issues raised by residents, including traffic congestion. The study is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027.

She said the study was important as Bukit Jalil had unique characteristics as an event and concert hub that generated heavy traffic, requiring a specialised traffic management approach compared with other areas.

“We know there is congestion. Every weekend, whenever there is a concert, Bukit Jalil becomes extremely congested. Traffic builds up hours before the concert even begins. I acknowledge the problem,” she said when winding up the debate on the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 at the committee stage for the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.

Hannah said the traffic management plan for Bukit Jalil was also expected to be completed by February 2027 and would be audited by Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) to ensure its implementation was effective on the ground and not merely a plan on paper.

As part of efforts to find long-term solutions, she said the Federal Territories Department would hold discussions with the Digital Ministry to explore opportunities to implement smart city solutions to help address congestion in the area.

In addition, Hannah said discussions were also being held with Prasarana Malaysia Bhd (Prasarana) to examine ways to improve public transport access to Bukit Jalil, including the possibility of establishing a bus transit hub in connection with the proposed Mass Rapid Transit 3 (MRT3) project.

On a related development, she said the development of Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil was subject to the provision of infrastructure beforehand or concurrently with the development to ensure that basic facilities could accommodate residents’ needs.

Hannah said four planning approvals had been granted, covering the overall layout development order, Madani Hub comprising a hall, food court and bus station, Residensi Madani homes priced below RM200,000 involving 4,218 units, and Sekolah Madani comprising preschool, primary and secondary schools as well as special education facilities.
“DBKL acts as the approving authority for this development. It will ensure that all development complies with the Kuala Lumpur Local Plan (PTKL) 2040, including population density requirements.
“The proposed development of Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil, with an estimated overall density of 1,048 people per acre, is in line with the affordable housing guidelines and PTKL 2040,” she said.

She said the Kuala Lumpur Mayor was monitoring the development to ensure that the necessary infrastructure was provided in tandem with the progress of the project before further planning approvals were granted for subsequent phases.

On pedestrian facilities, Hannah said DBKL would construct 22 kilometres (km) of pedestrian walkways in parliamentary constituencies across the capital, with an allocation of RM55 million, beginning in January 2027.
She said the project would involve the construction of two-kilometre walkways in each parliamentary constituency and was expected to be completed in the third quarter of next year.

“The construction of covered pedestrian walkways from 2023 to date has involved 29 locations, covering a total distance of 4.35 km. Currently, there are no pedestrian walkway projects under construction,” she said.

She added that DBKL was also planning an additional 20 km of covered pedestrian walkways in the city centre to connect public transport facilities with commercial centres, office complexes and recreational areas, including the Botanical Gardens and Titiwangsa Lake Gardens. — Bernama
bf77412e4d68125d: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has decided not to extradite prominent preacher Dr Zakir Naik to India and has made no commitment to hand him over to the country.

Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the decision was based on Malaysia's rights under Article 6 of the extradition treaty signed with the Indian government in 2010, as well as provisions under the Extradition Act 1992.
He said the government had not received any new extradition request from India concerning Zakir.
The Indian government had previously submitted an official extradition request on Jan 19, 2018, followed by a diplomatic note seeking a review of the decision on May 29, 2020.

"The Malaysian government has decided not to extradite Dr Zakir Naik to India. Therefore, no commitment has been made to extradite him," he said in a written reply published on the parliament website.

Saifuddin was responding to a question from Datuk Dr Ahmad Marzuk Shaary (PN-Pengkalan Chepa), who asked for the latest status of India's extradition request for Zakir, including the date the most recent official request was received.
Marzuk also sought clarification on whether the documents and evidence submitted met the requirements of the Extradition Act 1992 and the Malaysia-India extradition treaty.
He also asked whether the government had made any commitment regarding the preacher's extradition.

In September, media reports said the government had been urged to clarify the legal and diplomatic status of the extradition request, which was discussed by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi.

Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan was reported to have said that Anwar should also explain the issues discussed and the understanding reached during the meeting between the two leaders.
He said clarification was also needed on whether the evidence and documents submitted by New Delhi to Kuala Lumpur in support of the request met Malaysia's legal requirements for extradition.

The calls followed earlier media reports that Zakir's extradition, sought by India over allegations of money laundering and hate speech, was among the matters discussed during talks between Anwar and Indian representatives.
Indian news outlet New Delhi Television (NDTV) reported that Anwar had confirmed the matter was discussed behind closed doors, reportedly in New Delhi.
b45c2a25c89ab8d1: BRUSSELS: Grocery stores across at least nine European countries were hit Monday by a suspected cyberattack on their freezer systems, prompting the EU to warn of a deliberate attempt to disrupt the bloc's food supply chain.

Supermarkets in Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal and Sweden reported refrigeration problems that forced some retailers to discard food after temperatures rose overnight.
The incident came three weeks after a cyberattack disrupted French grocery stores and led hundreds of outlets to throw away spoilt stock.
No one has claimed responsibility for either incident.
EU food and agriculture commissioner Christophe Hansen said the bloc was taking the incidents "very seriously".
"They are a deliberate attempt to disrupt our food supply chain and undermine consumers' confidence in it – a warning that we must take seriously," Hansen said.

In Italy, at least four supermarkets in Sicily and one business in Tuscany were affected, according to media reports and the national cybersecurity agency. The Italian government was to hold a cybersecurity meeting with intelligence services on Tuesday.
Belgium was among the hardest-hit countries, with dozens of stores across several grocery chains reporting refrigeration failures. Federal prosecutors opened an investigation.
"It's a cyberattack; there is no other reason," said Mich Vergauwen, a spokesman for Carrefour Belgium, which reported disruption in about 15 of its 700 stores.
Carrefour Belgium said around 15 stores were affected, while Ikea said its Mons outlet also experienced a cyberattack that caused freezer temperatures to rise.

Belgian refrigeration company Sabcobel said it had begun securing its installations after the October attack in France, but some systems had yet to be upgraded and were among those affected on Monday.
Delhaize, Colruyt and Intermarche also reported refrigeration problems at stores in Belgium, while four Delhaize outlets in Luxembourg were affected.
In Ireland, retailer Musgrave said 13 Supervalu stores were impacted by what it described as a cyber incident.
A small number of corner shops in the Netherlands also suffered disruptions.

In Portugal, the Mosqueteiros group confirmed two AFP incidents at seven Intermarche stores linked to a cyberattack, which "appears to have targeted an external service provider responsible for managing the refrigeration systems."
And in Sweden, chain Coop confirmed six of its around 800 stores had been hit.
"We can confirm that it is a cyber incident. The problem has now been resolved and the fridges and freezers are working as normal," spokesman Carlos Cancino told AFP.
He said Coop did not know who was behind the attack but noted that the affected stores had been connected to a 4G mobile network, not the updated 5G system, which made them "more exposed" to hackers.
- 'Vulnerabilities' -
Swedish chain Ica also said "a limited number" of its stores experienced refrigeration problems, without confirming a cyberattack.

According to Ica spokesperson Helena Johansson, the affected stores were all connected to an external refrigeration control system provided by Danish manufacturer Danfoss – the same supplier targeted in the October 12 cyberattack on French retailers.
She referred all queries to Danfoss, which had yet to respond to an AFP request for a comment.
In Finland, irregular temperatures had also been detected in a few smaller grocery stores belonging to the Kesko group.
"We are currently investigating the cause, and interference via the network has not yet been ruled out," Petri Kayhko, head of Kesko's corporate security, told AFP.
Roni Kokkola, an information security specialist at the National Cyber Security Centre at Finland's Transport and Communications Agency Traficom, would not rule out cyber interference.
"We've seen this in Europe in the past few months, so it spreading beyond France to other countries has been expected," he told AFP.
"Nowadays it's very typical that all kinds of vulnerabilities are being exploited ever more actively and rapidly."
In Estonia, at least one supermarket was attacked by hackers who raised the temperature in the refrigeration units to 50°C, public broadcaster ERR reported.

The units were older models delivered by Danfoss, similar to the ones targeted in the France attack, Jann Mutso, director of Kitman Coldtech, a manufacturer and distributor of advanced refrigeration systems, told ERR.

d1275693f7d796de: WASHINGTON: The White House on Monday highlighted US President Donald Trump's trade agreement with South Korea and a Alaska natural gas project involving Seoul among his fulfilled campaign promises, as it touted his achievements on the eve of the US midterm elections, Yonhap News Agency reported.

1a17b126b3cde209: SAN FRANCISCO: Apple exceeded analysts' expectations for its latest results on Monday when the iPhone-maker said it notched a "revenue record" for the July-September quarter, driven by iPhone sales and services revenue, but increased costs related to AI will drag down margins.
"We're closing the year with our most ambitious lineup yet," CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook in September, said in a statement before speaking on a call with analysts Monday afternoon.
Ternus hinted at an optimistic outlook for sales of its latest products, including the foldable Duo, during the holiday season.
However, CFO Kevan Parekh warned that the company Apple's gross margin will slow a bit in the final stretch of the year, compared to its September quarter margin of 47.9 per cent.
"We expect gross margin to be between 45 per cent and 46 per cent. This includes primarily the impact of higher memory costs, as well as some costs related to the ramp of Siri AI," Parekh said.
In June, the company overhauled Siri, its digital assistant, through a partnership with Google, whose Gemini model was used to beef up the new Siri AI.
Apple tried to assuage investors' concerns about rising AI costs.

"We feel AI offers a compelling reason for customers to upgrade and switch in order to get the latest capabilities, and we also feel there are opportunities across third-party apps and partnerships as well as first-party opportunities," Parekh said.
Apple launched three new phones in September – the 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max and its first folding phone called the Duo – in addition to two new desktop computers.
In October, it also unveiled a new smart display powered by Siri AI called HomeView, as well as a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen for the first time.
In July, the company also launched Apple Upgrade, a leasing programme that lets US customers pay for an iPhone or other devices in monthly installments.
-Chips crunch-
Long criticised for falling behind in the AI race, Apple stands to benefit from the heavy spending of its peers on data centres while keeping its own investments lean.
Analysts expected the Cupertino giant to spend US$11 billion in the 12 months that ended in September, when its fiscal year ends.

That's a fraction of the annual expenditures of Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta, which are on track to spend more than US$700 billion on capital investment this year – roughly the size of Argentina's or Belgium's entire economy – much of it on AI infrastructure, according to analyst estimates.
In July, Meta said it expected to spend US$145 billion this year, nearly double what it spent in 2026.
Last week, Amazon said it expects to spend US$220 billion this year, and Microsoft said it expected to spend US$170 billion by the end of the year.
Alphabet's latest forecast for spending is between US$195 billion to US$205 billion in 2026.
The iPhone maker is in a legal battle with one of its close AI partners, though.
In July, Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly orchestrating a campaign to steal the iPhone maker's trade secrets as the AI lab tries to develop its own consumer hardware device.
OpenAI's flagship product, ChatGPT, has been integrated into Apple products since 2024.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
06f4003ab6f628b3: KUALA LUMPUR: The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) is projected to generate RM418 million in operating revenue in 2029 from passenger and freight services.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the projection comprised RM204 million from passenger services and RM214 million from freight operations.
He said a study conducted by consultants in 2025 projected passenger revenue of RM192 million in 2027, rising to RM198 million in 2028.
"Freight revenue is projected at RM68 million in 2027 and RM71 million in 2028, before increasing to RM214 million in 2029.
"These projections are subject to actual operational performance, including passenger numbers, freight volumes and changes in market demand," he said.

Loke was responding to a question from Datuk Wan Saifulruddin Wan Jan (PN-Tasek Gelugor), who sought details on the total construction cost of the ECRL, the annual payments the government would have to bear to finance its construction, estimated annual operating revenue and measures to ensure the sustainability of its operating costs.
His reply was published in a written response on the parliament website yesterday.
Freight services expected to drive revenue
Loke said the ECRL's long-term business model was based on a combination of revenue from freight and passenger services.
About 70 per cent of projected revenue would come from freight services, while the remaining 30 per cent would be generated by passenger services.

He said this approach would enable the ECRL to capitalise not only on passenger travel demand, but also on the potential movement of goods between the east and west coasts, as well as access to the country's major ports.
"To ensure operational sustainability, revenue from both services will be used to cover operating, maintenance and related costs.
"At the same time, ECRL Operation Sdn Bhd (EOSB), as the operator, will optimise non-fare revenue through commercial activities such as space rentals, advertising and other suitable sources.
"This joint venture model also involves sharing operational risks between the two shareholders to increase revenue, optimise asset utilisation and manage operating costs prudently," he said.
On a related matter, Loke said the construction cost of the 665km ECRL project, which runs from Kota Bharu to Port Klang, was RM52.43 billion.

He said the project was financed through several sources, including a term loan from China EXIM Bank (CEXIM), sukuk issued by Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL), development allocations from the Transport Ministry and financing from the Finance Ministry.
"As a large-scale strategic infrastructure project, the ECRL should not be assessed solely on the direct financial returns from its operations.
"Its long-term benefits and wider economic spillover effects for the country must also be taken into account," he said.
eeeb933b3e13587a: WASHINGTON, Nov 3 — The Kennedy Centre, the famed Washington arts hub that President Donald Trump has sought to overhaul, yesterday named singer Paul Anka and actor Andy Garcia among five honourees recognised for lifetime artist contributions.

The Kennedy Centre had long enjoyed bipartisan support before Trump appointed himself board chairman in February 2025, pledging to end “woke political programming” at the site.

6c0e24a69b2855fb: WASHINGTON: A group representing General Motors, Toyota, Volkswagen and other major automakers on Monday backed the Trump administration in a legal challenge to its sharply lower vehicle fuel economy standards filed by California and other states.

Last month, the US Transportation Department said it was finalising a fleet-wide fuel economy average of 34.9 miles per ⁠gallon (14.7 km per litre) by 2031, down from 50.4 miles per gallon (21.4 km per litre) that had been approved under then-President Joe Biden in 2024.

The Alliance for Automotive Innovation, which represents GM, Toyota, Volkswagen, Hyundai, Ford, Stellantis and other major automakers, backed the effort by President Donald Trump's administration after California, New York and two dozen other states, cities and counties sued last month.
"Automakers require certainty and stability in the standards," the group said in the filing with the 1st US Circuit Court of Appeals.

It added that if the standards were set aside, it "would affect automakers' business, endangering the capital investment planning, product development, and performance validation for hundreds of new vehicle models intended for the US market."

The states said the Trump administration was ignoring the presence of millions of electric vehicles, "leading to a ‌flawed, dramatically ⁠distorted analysis of the 'maximum feasible' fuel economy level." The automaker group said the court should reject those arguments.

The revised Trump administration standards seek to reverse Biden's push toward greater fuel efficiency and electric vehicles. A coalition of environmental ​and consumer groups also filed a separate lawsuit challenging the new rules.
The Transportation Department said the regulation reduces manufacturers' average cost per ​vehicle to comply by US$1,289 but increases fuel costs by more than US$1,600 over the vehicles' lifetime. ⁠
The department said the rule would increase US gasoline consumption through 2050 by 4.6 per cent, or about 121 billion gallons, compared with the Biden rules but also boost new car sales.

The American Petroleum Institute, an oil and natural gas industry trade group, also filed in support of the Trump administration's rules, saying they ensure the government sets standards that "do not force consumers to purchase vehicles that consume less fuel than they would otherwise choose."
991aa8cd1a99ae4e: SINGAPORE: Binance's customers have withdrawn a net US$4.72 billion from the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange since it reopened, after hackers stole around US$6.3 billion of crypto from the platform in what could be the largest-ever financial heist.
The exchange froze withdrawals for more than two days after the hack, which the FBI said was carried out by North Korea, then started allowing customers to withdraw again on Sunday morning.
The theft has underlined the vulnerability of digital assets to attacks and raised questions about the impact of the hack on Binance, which has vowed to repay customers in full.

Binance said the net outflows amounted to around 3.0 per cent of the assets on its platform, a relatively modest figure that analysts said suggested customer confidence had largely held up. Most withdrawals from the platform were in the form of Tether's USDT stablecoin, Binance added.

The outflow compares with about US$7 billion withdrawn from Circle's USDC stablecoin over a week after the collapse of Silicon Valley Bank in 2023. Binance itself processed net outflows of about US$6 billion over 72 hours in 2022 after the collapse of FTX.
The attack marks a step-up in North Korea's crypto thefts. Blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs said North Korea-linked hackers have stolen US$7.4 billion so far in 2026.

Analysts and crypto experts said the fallout appeared limited so far, and there was little sign of an impact on broader financial markets despite deepening ties between crypto and mainstream finance in recent years.
"Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not our users," the company said in a statement on X.
Binance said it was covering the losses with company funds and had already raised US$6 billion from its corporate treasury, an insurance fund and reserves set aside for security breaches.
"It has not yet triggered widespread panic or a massive, concentrated withdrawal," said Tim Sun, a senior researcher at HashKey Group, a digital asset financial service company in Hong Kong.

Binance, which says it has more than 335 million users worldwide and average daily trading volumes of US$95 billion across digital assets and derivatives, said it had also seen US$2.7 billion in customer inflows since Sunday and that withdrawal volumes were stabilising after an "initial spike."

Data from data analytics provider DeFiLlama showed several crypto exchanges received notable inflows to their platforms since Binance opened withdrawals, although it was unclear what share came from users moving funds off Binance.

OKX recorded US$284.87 million in inflows in the last 24 hours, followed by Gate with US$93.22 million in inflows and Bybit, which saw US$29.25 million in inflows. Representatives for OKX, Gate and Bybit did not respond to requests for comment.
NO RUSH TO WITHDRAW
Some traders told Reuters they were keeping their accounts on Binance.
Ryan Tan, a Binance user, said he was in no hurry to withdraw his funds from the platform, as he had already kept his account fairly light since the collapse of FTX four years ago.
"After the FTX collapse, I decided to hold everything on my wallet instead of leaving them on exchanges," said the 39-year-old.
After hitting a six-week low on Friday, bitcoin prices recovered through the weekend to trade above US$77,000 on Monday, while ether also rebounded from a two-month low.

Stablecoin market capitalisations, often viewed as a gauge of money moving into and out of crypto markets, have fallen since Friday, suggesting some investors have shifted funds into cash or traditional assets. Binance started allowing US dollar cash withdrawals again on Monday.
"HIGHLY COMPLEX" MONEY LAUNDERING

The FBI said on Saturday that the North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor was responsible for the attack. Researchers describe the group as highly sophisticated and say its activities help fund the country's weapons programmes.

Analysts said the attack's scale could curb institutional appetite for cryptocurrencies. Spot bitcoin ETFs recorded outflows of US$643 million on Friday, the largest daily withdrawal in October, while more than US$1.3 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated, according to Ari Redbord, global head of policy at TRM Labs.
"A hack at a crypto exchange is bank robbery at the speed of the internet, which creates an unstable risk profile for anyone responsible for other people's capital," he said.
About half of the stolen funds were held in stablecoins and have been frozen by issuers, including Circle, which said on Monday it had frozen more than US$1.1 billion in USDC.

According to blockchain analytics firm Elliptic, the hackers still control around US$3.28 billion, mostly in bitcoin and ether, and only a negligible amount has been cashed out of crypto and into fiat currency. Elliptic described the laundering process as "highly complex and clearly automated".

Jonathan Benton, founder and chief executive at crypto asset recovery firm iSanctuary, said blockchain technology exists to trace stolen funds, but the challenge is turning that intelligence into rapid, coordinated action before those assets disappear.

"The future of crypto won't be decided by how much money enters the market but by how safe that money is once it's there," said Benton, former head of the international corruption unit of the UK's National Crime Agency.

843da333b031cbff: WASHINGTON: US secretary of state Marco Rubio met with Venezuela's foreign minister Oliver Blanco on Monday, calling for the release of more political prisoners jailed under deposed leader Nicolas Maduro as part of the country's political transition.

The meeting marked Blanco's US first visit after being named to his post last week by interim president Delcy Rodriguez, who has led Venezuela under Washington's oversight since American forces ousted Maduro in January.

"Secretary Rubio reaffirmed the President's three-phase plan for Venezuela: stabilisation,q economic recovery and political reconciliation, and democratic transition," a State Department readout of the meeting said.
The diplomats posed together in front of the press briefly before the meeting, though neither gave a statement.
"The two discussed progress in the Venezuelan-led reconciliation talks, including institutional reforms that lay the groundwork for free, fair, and credible elections," the readout added.
"Secretary Rubio urged the continued release of the remaining political prisoners in Venezuela," it continued.

Maduro, who had led Venezuela since 2013 with an increasingly authoritarian bent, was widely accused of arresting political opponents and other activists, often on trumped-up charges of coup plotting.
Washington has pressed for the release of political prisoners since Rodriguez assumed power, with a landmark amnesty law leading to the release of many, though hundreds remain behind bars.
The most recent tally from NGO Foro Penal, which defends political prisoners, said there were 344 such prisoners in Venezuela as of Sept 18.
After a series of talks, both the Venezuelan government and opposition figures have said that Venezuela will hold fresh elections, without providing details on when they will take place.

Blanco also met with US treasury secretary Scott Bessent, with whom he "discussed developments in Venezuela and opportunities to advance the Trump Administration's three-phase approach of stabilisation, recovery, and transition", according to a US readout.
3a23ae70322cd782: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Strong cooperation and a close working relationship between the Federal Government and the Sarawak government have delivered high-impact transport development projects in the state within a short period, says Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook.
He said close cross-party cooperation with his deputy, Datuk Hasbi Habibollah, has allowed several major commitments to be fulfilled for the people of Sarawak.

Key achievements include solid support in realising Sarawak’s own boutique airline, the handover of Bintulu Port Authority to the state government, the introduction of the BAS.MY public transport system in Kuching, the Miri Airport upgrading project, and the construction of a new Road Transport Department (JPJ) complex in Limbang.
“Over the past few years, since we teamed up at the Transport Ministry, Datuk Hasbi and I have worked together closely without any issues, despite coming from different political backgrounds.

“We have always maintained a very good working relationship, and as a result, we have been able to implement and resolve many matters,” he said in a video recording of his speech at the groundbreaking ceremony for the Limbang JPJ branch office on Oct 28, uploaded to his Facebook page yesterday.
Touching on the establishment of Sarawak’s airline, Loke said the goal was achieved in less than three years through strategic cooperation between both sides.

“For Sarawak, we have jointly delivered on several major matters at the Transport Ministry. First, during this term alone, we helped realise the Sarawak government’s aspiration to have its own airline,” he said.

He explained that AirBorneo has commenced operations and taken over MASwings services, with all ATR aircraft now under AirBorneo, alongside plans to operate jet aircraft connecting Sarawak to various regional destinations.
Beyond aviation, Loke said the Federal Government also fulfilled demands under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) by returning port authority powers to the state.
On land transport, Loke said the ministry expanded the public transport network by providing direct funding to Sarawak, which the state had never received previously.
“At the departmental level, we started the BAS.MY service in Kuching, a key initiative by the Transport Ministry given that Sarawak never had a federally funded stage bus system before.

“Starting in Kuching, we hope to expand this service to other areas in the future. As for the JPJ, this is the only new building construction approved for this term, and we will assess needs in other locations after this,” he said.

Meanwhile, addressing connectivity in northern Sarawak, Loke said the expansion and upgrading of Miri Airport has been approved by the Ministry of Finance to cope with passenger overflow and spur economic growth in surrounding areas, including the Limbang Division.

“This project serves as an important gateway to Limbang, and I am confident its capacity can be increased. This will allow for more flights, bringing more visitors here, which is vital to stimulate development across Limbang,” he said. — Bernama
da399e3980adde99: SYDNEY: Australia's landmark social media ban faces a legal test on Tuesday, as online platform Reddit urges the nation's highest court to scrap the world-leading restrictions.
Social media companies have been forced to purge millions of accounts after Australia banned under-16s from the likes of Facebook, TikTok and Reddit last December.
The High Court of Australia will sit on Tuesday and Wednesday as Reddit, one of the most popular websites in the world, argues the laws are misguided and should be overturned.
Reddit has highlighted a number of issues in its written submission to the court, pointing to problems enforcing the ban and a lack of scientific evidence about the harms of social media.
"The evidence so far is that the effectiveness of the ban has been limited," reads Reddit's submission.
Australia's ban works by restricting children under 16 from holding accounts on the world's biggest social media platforms.
These platforms are responsible for weeding out underage users and face hefty fines if they are found to be falling short of their obligations.
Reddit argued this approach was actually more dangerous, as registered accounts were governed by in-built safety features.
Material posted on many online platforms and social media sites could still be accessed without an account, Reddit said.
"Young people using other platforms without an account are also unable to be protected from exposure to particular harmful content as they previously had been," its submission read.
Australia said its restrictions would protect young users from graphic content, online predators and predatory algorithms designed to keep people scrolling.
While there is a growing body of evidence about the harms of social media, Reddit argued there was no "scientific consensus".
Political discourse
Reddit, which has also argued it should be exempt from the ban, said there was little research on whether certain platforms were safer than others.
The High Court will also consider arguments from Australia's Digital Freedom Project, which believes the ban restricts teens' ability to take part in political discourse.
"Social media is an important means of accessing news and engaging in political communication for young Australians, including children under 16," the advocacy group argued in written submissions.
"The restriction also risks removing beneficial sources of connection, support and participation," it added.
Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project separately announced last year they would challenge the ban.
It was not clear how long it would take the high court to consider the case, although even the quickest decisions typically take months.
Social media firms face mounting scrutiny over their use of allegedly addictive algorithms and stand accused of directing users to extreme content to keep them scrolling.
Several countries have indicated an interest in following Australia's lead, including New Zealand, the UK, France and Turkey.
A team of Australia-based researchers published a study earlier this year that found little evidence to suggest teenagers have turned away from social media as a consequence of the restrictions.
9f63cb5eabcc102f: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is prepared to study a proposal to establish a special fund for environmental rehabilitation following haze incidents.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said further discussions would be held with the relevant ministries and agencies.
The study would take into account existing assistance mechanisms, actual needs and the financial implications for the government.
He said funding mechanisms for haze management should not focus solely on rehabilitation after an incident, but should cover the entire risk management cycle.
This includes prevention, the use of monitoring technology, peatland management, early firefighting, research and the rehabilitation of affected areas.
"The government is prepared to study the need for and appropriate funding mechanisms. This matter requires further consideration with the relevant ministries and agencies.
"The government believes that funding mechanisms for haze should not focus solely on post-incident rehabilitation, but should also support the entire risk management cycle," he said.

Arthur was responding to a question from Dr Ahmad Fakhruddin Fakhrurazi (PN-Kuala Kedah) on the country's long-term preparedness plan for transboundary haze and the proposal to establish a special post-haze environmental rehabilitation fund.
His response was contained in a written reply published on the parliament website.
On regional efforts, Arthur said Malaysia also supported strengthening the Asean Transboundary Haze Pollution Control Fund, also known as the Asean Haze Fund.
This includes efforts to broaden its sources of contributions and expand the scope of its use.
He said the fund could support scientific research, capacity-building, preventive innovations, firefighting efforts and science diplomacy.
To improve early warnings of air pollution in high-risk areas, the Environment Department (DOE) continuously monitors air quality through 68 automatic monitoring stations nationwide.
Arthur said the stations measured concentrations of air pollutants, allowing the Air Pollutant Index (API) to be monitored and reported continuously.
This would help authorities detect rising pollution levels at an earlier stage.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) also provides information through the Fire Danger Rating System (FDRS) for Malaysia and the Asean region.
The system assesses and monitors forest and peatland fire risks based on weather conditions and environmental factors.
"The system provides fire risk forecasts up to seven days ahead, helping relevant agencies identify areas at risk of fire and implement preparedness and early prevention measures.
"MetMalaysia also developed and launched the Malaysian Community Multiscale Air Quality Model (MyCMAQ) on March 31.
"It provides regular, high-resolution forecasts of air quality conditions and atmospheric pollutant concentrations in Malaysia and Southeast Asia," he said.
Arthur said the integrated use of the three systems enabled the government to monitor changes in air quality, identify areas at high risk of fires and anticipate potential haze pollution.
The information also served as a basis for coordinating preventive measures, field monitoring, enforcement and public health advisories.
These efforts were particularly important in areas at risk of forest and peatland fires, as well as transboundary haze.

ad7161a15e09498c: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Some 10,036 patients in Malaysia are living with organ failure as of Oct 15, highlighting the need for comprehensive reforms to the country’s organ donation and transplant system to improve access to life-saving treatment.

“Through MTK, we are bringing together ministries and agencies to improve coordination. This includes emergency air transport through Mercy Flight, involving the Fire and Rescue Department and the Defence Ministry, as well as police Outrider escorts to minimise delays.

“We are also studying a proposal to include organ donor registration status on driving licences in collaboration with the Transport Ministry. This would be supported by sustainable funding from the Finance Ministry and clear religious guidance from the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM),” he said in a Facebook post.
Dzulkefly said he had chaired the first MTK meeting yesterday afternoon.
He said the reforms would bring three main benefits, including ensuring that organs were allocated more transparently and fairly based on medical priorities.
They would also give the public greater confidence in organ donation, with all procedures governed by the Human Tissues Act 1974 and relevant religious rulings.
“The integrated logistics network will also ensure that donated organs reach operating theatres as quickly as possible,” he said.

Dzulkefly said the Health Ministry would continue to strengthen public awareness campaigns through the “Warisku, Hormati Ikrarku” initiative to ensure donors’ wishes were respected, including by their family members.
He said respecting donors’ pledges and supporting patients awaiting transplants were a shared responsibility. — Bernama

6a731df3b9ccfb29: KYIV, (Ukraine): Ukraine said Monday that Russian strikes on a school distributing humanitarian aid killed at least 26 people, dashing fragile hopes of "progress toward peace" after a local ceasefire in the south expired without violations.

Russia resumed its strikes on the southern region of Kherson after the end of a ceasefire in the area, the longest truce in the war raging between the neighbours since Russia's 2022 invasion, Kyiv said.

A rare pause in the fighting, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump to enable a mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, ended Sunday after starting on Tuesday, with neither side reporting breaches.
But hours after the truce, Russia targeted a village in Zaporizhzhia, adjacent to Kherson, with repeated strikes that killed at least 26 people, the acting regional governor said.
Some of the dead had come to collect aid at a local school.
Footage posted by the Ukrainian emergency services showed the building reduced to piles of smouldering rubble and rescuers working at the site.
"Every Monday, humanitarian aid was distributed to people there," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in his daily address.
"The Russians carried out the first strike just as people arrived — several aerial bombs. Then, there was a repeat strike — more aerial bombs, this time targeting the shelter."
Among those killed were "two rescue workers and four police officers", acting regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said on Telegram.
The service named the rescuers as two 44-year-olds: Denys Konovalenko and Oleksy Sushchevsky.
"Every day, they went out to help people, working in dangerous conditions and risking their own lives to save others," it said in a statement.
Zelenskyy said that after the Oleshky truce, "there was a moment when the next steps could have shown that progress toward peace was possible."
"With these killings, Russia is sending an entirely opposite signal: Russia is counting on more killings. There must be a response to this."
- Russia fortifies positions -
The ceasefire last week enabled an evacuation of the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.
It was the longest pause in fighting between the neighbours in the war, which is grinding through its fifth year after killing hundreds of thousands of people and displacing millions.
A senior Ukrainian figure told AFP on Sunday that Russia refused a Ukrainian offer to extend the truce.
Kyiv's military also alleged that Moscow had used the pause in fighting to "fortify its positions."
The Kremlin did not deny the accusations, with its spokesman Dmitry Peskov telling reporters Monday: "This is a completely normal practice in such situations."
He alleged the Ukrainian army had also used pauses in fighting in the past to regroup.

Moscow saw the Oleshky humanitarian mission as "successful", Peskov added, praising the "good cooperation between all sides" and singling out the role of its human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova.
Lantratova oversaw the ceasefire alongside her Ukrainian counterpart Dmytro Lubinets in one of the most substantial instances of Russian-Ukrainian cooperation since the start of the war.
The mission saw people evacuated to both Ukraine-controlled territory and Moscow-annexed Crimea.
The Kremlin said that no other similar missions were being planned "at the moment."
US-led talks between Russia and Ukraine are set to resume next week, US special envoy Steve Witkoff said Monday.
President Donald Trump has pushed for a settlement to the dragging war but there has been no breakthrough.
The talks — to be held Nov 10 and 11 in Abu Dhabi, Witkoff said — come as Kyiv and its European allies worry that Trump has increasingly sided with Moscow.
- Cyberattacks -
Both Russia and Ukraine said overnight that their emergency warnings apps were hacked in apparent cyberattacks that came hours after the truce had ended.
Ukraine said it suspected its air raid alert system had been compromised, after false alerts of a radiation threat were sent to millions.
The warning system provides vital information about incoming Russian drones and missiles.
Russia has intensified its attacks this year, firing ballistic missiles and fast jet-powered drones, both of which are hard to intercept.
Moscow said that an app belonging to its emergency situations ministry that also warns of attacks had been hacked, too.
The app is not widely used in Russia, where warnings of Ukrainian drone attacks are not as common and typically sent by text message in border regions. — AFP
